# Overview {-}

**Question.** What is the cellular-component make-up of the insoluble skeletal-muscle proteome in adult and old mice, and do the age-related changes in composition, abundance and protein detection differ between females and males?

**Design.** Gastrocnemius, control mice only; Age (Adult, Old) × Sex (Female, Male). Sample sizes are printed in *Load data*. Every protein is assigned to **one** GO Cellular Component bin and the same preprocessing and reproducibility filter are used throughout. Results are given twice:

1. **Combined analysis:** Female and Male samples pooled within Adult and Old.
2. **Sex-resolved analysis:** Adult Female, Old Female, Adult Male and Old Male kept separate, with Female- and Male-specific abundance and detection summaries.

> **Scope.** The Age, Sex and Age × Sex tests in this report are **composition-level tests of cellular-component fractions**. Protein-level differential abundance (limma) is in the separate Insoluble report (script 2) and is not repeated here.

**Methods in brief**

| Step | What is done |
|---|---|
| Samples | Control animals, Adult or Old, Female or Male, present in the intensity table |
| Detection | A protein is *detected* in a sample when its raw intensity is > 0; missing and non-positive values are non-detections. Raw (non-log) intensities are used for abundance weighting. |
| GO-CC bins | The first listed gene symbol is annotated; each prespecified GO root is expanded with `GOCCOFFSPRING`; a protein gets the **first matching bin** in a fixed priority order. Unmatched proteins ("Other/Unassigned") are excluded from all bin-based analyses. |
| Reproducibility filter | Keep a protein detected in **≥ 2 Adult OR ≥ 2 Old** samples (sexes pooled within age) |
| Composition | **Abundance-weighted:** summed raw intensity of a bin ÷ total of all assigned, filtered proteins in that sample. **Count-weighted:** detected proteins in a bin ÷ all detected, assigned, filtered proteins. |
| Composition tests | Per-sample fractions are arcsine-square-root transformed. Combined: `Fraction_asin ~ Age`. Factorial: `Fraction_asin ~ Age * Sex`, Type III *F* tests with sum-to-zero contrasts. Benjamini–Hochberg FDR across bins, separately for Age, Sex and Age × Sex. |
| Summed raw abundance | Per mouse and bin, summed raw intensity; tests on `log2(sum)` with the same 2 × 2 model; Female- and Male-specific Old − Adult contrasts from `emmeans` (unadjusted *P*). BH across the eight displayed bins. |
| Effect sizes | **Percentage-point:** Old − Adult in % of total insoluble abundance. **Within-bin relative:** `100 × (Old − Adult) / Adult`. 95 % percentile bootstrap CIs (5,000 resamples within age, fixed seeds). These are composition effect sizes, not protein-level effects. |
| Protein summaries | Mean and median abundance among **positive detections only**; detection counts and prevalence are reported alongside |
| Detection tests | Two-sided Fisher exact test of Adult vs Old detection per protein (pooled, and within each sex); BH across proteins within each analysis. Categories: **Old-only** (Old ≥ 2, Adult = 0), **Adult-only** (Adult ≥ 2, Old = 0), **Old-predominant** (Old ≥ 2, Adult ≤ 1). |

**How to read the figures.** ER and Ribosome are omitted from several multi-panel figures because each is represented by one retained protein; they stay in the denominator, so the displayed fractions are **not** renormalized. Centered abundance displays subtract each protein's own across-group mean `log10` abundance and must not be used to compare absolute abundance between proteins. A protein that is Old-predominant in only one sex is a **descriptive** detection pattern, not evidence of an Age × Sex interaction; distance from the diagonal in the detection scatter is likewise not an interaction test.

**Outputs.** Everything is written under `Comp_AO/` (`Shared/`, `Combined/`, `SexSplit/`); PNG and editable SVG with separate legends. The folder layout is listed in *Output guide*.

> **To run:** keep the two input CSV files (see *Settings*) and the `R/` folder next to this file, then knit. Code is folded by default; use the **Code** buttons to expand it.

# Setup

## Packages

All packages must be installed beforehand (the script stops and lists any that are missing). Package load order is kept identical to the original analysis because it determines which functions mask which.

```{r packages}
pkgs <- c("tidyverse", "scales", "viridisLite", "ggtext", "ggrepel", "patchwork", "ragg",
          "car", "emmeans", "AnnotationDbi", "org.Mm.eg.db", "GO.db", "svglite")
missing_pkgs <- pkgs[!vapply(pkgs, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) {
  stop("Install missing packages first: ", paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
}
invisible(lapply(pkgs[1:12], library, character.only = TRUE))
select <- dplyr::select   # AnnotationDbi masks dplyr::select
```

## Figure export settings (presentation only)

Panel sizes (mm), font sizes (pt) and line/point sizes for the exported PNG/SVG files. Editing them changes only how figures are drawn and saved, never the statistics. Each panel ID is the exact PNG/SVG file name. The export functions live in `R/nm_export_engine_comp_AO.R`.

The panel sizes approximate the placed artwork in **Figure 3** (180 × 225 mm page): `Mass_2x2` (a), `Count_2x2` (b), `Mass_2x2_noSarcoCyto_originalTotal` (c), `RawBin_2x2` (d), `RawBin_AgeEffects_E2` (e), `Top10_PooledOldRank_bySex_4Groups` (i) and `DetectionDelta_Female_vs_Male` (j); the microscopy panels f–h are not made here. To resize a figure after it has been generated, change its entry in `nm_dims`, run **this chunk only**, then call `reexport("Mass_2x2")` (or another ID). No model refitting is needed. Sizes embedded in a plotted layer (bar outlines, bubble sizes) need the plotting chunk to be rerun first.

## Helper functions

```{r helpers}
# Shared PNG/SVG export; preserves the original (plot, file, width, height) API.
save_plot_png <- function(plot, file, width, height, dpi = 300) {
  nm_save_plot(plot, file, width, height, dpi)
}

fmt_p <- function(p) {
  dplyr::case_when(is.na(p) ~ "NA", p < 0.001 ~ "<0.001", TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", p))
}

# Compact facet labels for eight-panel (4 x 2) composition figures. The
# Interaction P/FDR results are retained in the statistical data tables,
# but not printed in the Figure 3 composition-grid facet headers.
# A = Age; S = Sex; p = raw p-value; FDR = BH-adjusted p-value.
nm_short_bin_name <- function(x) {
  map <- c(
    "Sarcomere/Myofibril" = "Sarcomere",
    "Plasma membrane" = "Plasma mem.",
    "Mitochondrion" = "Mitochondria"
  )
  x <- as.character(x)
  y <- unname(map[x])
  y[is.na(y)] <- x[is.na(y)]
  y
}

nm_comp_strip_label <- function(bin, p_Age, p_Sex, p_AgeSex, FDR_Age, FDR_Sex, FDR_AgeSex) {
  # Age and Sex only, exactly as Figure 3d; the statistical calculations
  # still retain Age x Sex P/FDR values in tables for the manuscript.
  paste0(
    "<b><span style='font-size:", nm_style$strip_text, "pt;'>",
    nm_short_bin_name(bin), "</span></b><br>",
    "<span style='font-size:", nm_style$strip_stats, "pt;'>",
    "p: A=", fmt_p(p_Age), " S=", fmt_p(p_Sex), "<br>",
    "FDR: A=", fmt_p(FDR_Age), " S=", fmt_p(FDR_Sex),
    "</span>"
  )
}

fmt_p_detection <- function(p) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(p) ~ "p=NA",
    p < 0.001 ~ "p<0.001*",
    p <= 0.050 ~ paste0("p=", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3), "*"),
    TRUE ~ paste0("p=", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3))
  )
}
```
# Load data and select Adult/Old controls

```{r load-data}
df <- read.csv(intensity_file, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

meta <- read.csv(meta_file, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

required_meta <- c("ID", "Age", "Treatment", "Sex")
missing_meta <- setdiff(required_meta, colnames(meta))

if (length(missing_meta) > 0) {
  stop("Missing metadata columns: ", paste(missing_meta, collapse = ", "))
}

required_df <- c("Protein.Group", "Genes")
missing_df <- setdiff(required_df, colnames(df))

if (length(missing_df) > 0) {
  stop("Missing protein-data columns: ", paste(missing_df, collapse = ", "))
}

ctrl <- meta %>%
  mutate(
    ID = as.character(ID),
    Treatment = str_to_title(trimws(as.character(Treatment))),
    Age = str_to_title(trimws(as.character(Age))),
    Sex = str_to_title(trimws(as.character(Sex)))
  ) %>%
  filter(Treatment == "Control", Age %in% c("Adult", "Old"), ID %in% colnames(df)) %>%
  mutate(
    Age = factor(Age, levels = c("Adult", "Old")),
    Sex = factor(Sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    Group_2x2 = factor(
      paste(Age, Sex, sep = "_"),
      levels = c("Adult_Female", "Old_Female", "Adult_Male", "Old_Male")
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(Age, Sex, ID)

if (nrow(ctrl) < 4) {
  stop("Too few Adult/Old Control samples were found.")
}

all_cols <- ctrl$ID

cat("Samples included:\n")
print(table(ctrl$Age, ctrl$Sex))
```
# Build long-format intensity table

Raw intensities are retained for composition weighting. Zeros and missing values are treated as non-detections with intensity zero.

The first gene symbol in the `Genes` field is used for GO annotation; `Protein.Group` remains the unique protein identity.

```{r long-table}
mat_raw <- df %>%
  select(Protein.Group, Genes, all_of(all_cols)) %>%
  mutate(
    Protein.Group = as.character(Protein.Group),
    Genes = as.character(Genes),
    Gene1 = str_trim(str_remove(Genes, ";.*$")),
    Gene1 = if_else(is.na(Gene1) | Gene1 == "", Protein.Group, Gene1)
  )

long <- mat_raw %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(all_cols), names_to = "Sample", values_to = "Intensity") %>%
  mutate(
    Intensity = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Intensity)),
    Intensity = if_else(is.na(Intensity) | Intensity <= 0, 0, Intensity)
  ) %>%
  left_join(ctrl %>% select(ID, Age, Sex, Group_2x2), by = c("Sample" = "ID"))
```
# GO Cellular Component single-bin assignment

```{r go-cc-assignment}
bin_roots <- list(
  "ECM"                 = c("GO:0031012"),
  "Extracellular"       = c("GO:0005576"),
  "Sarcomere/Myofibril" = c("GO:0030017", "GO:0030016", "GO:0043292"),
  "Cytoskeleton"        = c("GO:0005856"),
  "Mitochondrion"       = c("GO:0005739"),
  "Nucleus"             = c("GO:0005634"),
  "Ribosome"            = c("GO:0005840"),
  "ER"                  = c("GO:0005783"),
  "Golgi"               = c("GO:0005794"),
  "Plasma membrane"     = c("GO:0005886"),
  "Endosome/Lysosome"   = c("GO:0005768", "GO:0005764"),
  "Proteasome"          = c("GO:0000502"),
  "Cytosol"             = c("GO:0005829")
)

bin_priority <- names(bin_roots)

go_cc_offspring <- AnnotationDbi::as.list(GO.db::GOCCOFFSPRING)

get_offspring <- function(go_id) {
  kids <- go_cc_offspring[[go_id]]
  unique(c(go_id, kids))
}

bin_terms <- lapply(
  bin_roots,
  function(ids) {
    unique(unlist(lapply(ids, get_offspring), use.names = FALSE))
  }
)

assign_bin <- function(go_vec) {
  go_vec <- unique(go_vec[!is.na(go_vec)])

  if (length(go_vec) == 0) {
    return("Other/Unassigned")
  }

  for (b in bin_priority) {
    if (any(go_vec %in% bin_terms[[b]])) {
      return(b)
    }
  }

  "Other/Unassigned"
}

genes <- sort(unique(na.omit(long$Gene1)))

gene2entrez <- suppressMessages(
  AnnotationDbi::select(org.Mm.eg.db, keys = genes, keytype = "SYMBOL", columns = c("SYMBOL", "ENTREZID"))
) %>%
  distinct(SYMBOL, ENTREZID) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ENTREZID))

entrez2go <- suppressMessages(
  AnnotationDbi::select(
    org.Mm.eg.db,
    keys = sort(unique(gene2entrez$ENTREZID)),
    keytype = "ENTREZID",
    columns = c("ENTREZID", "GO", "ONTOLOGY")
  )
) %>%
  filter(ONTOLOGY == "CC", !is.na(GO)) %>%
  distinct(ENTREZID, GO)

gene_bin <- gene2entrez %>%
  left_join(entrez2go, by = "ENTREZID") %>%
  group_by(SYMBOL) %>%
  summarise(GO_CC = list(unique(GO)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Bin = vapply(GO_CC, assign_bin, character(1)))

long <- long %>%
  left_join(gene_bin %>% select(SYMBOL, Bin), by = c("Gene1" = "SYMBOL")) %>%
  mutate(Bin = if_else(is.na(Bin), "Other/Unassigned", Bin))

write.csv(
  long %>%
    distinct(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin),
  file.path(shared_dir, "Protein_GOCC_bin_assignment.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("GO-CC assignment before removing unassigned proteins:\n")
print(long %>% distinct(Protein.Group, Bin) %>% count(Bin, sort = TRUE))

long_assigned <- long %>%
  filter(Bin != "Other/Unassigned")
```
# Reproducibility filter

A protein is retained if it is detected in at least two Adult samples **or** at least two Old samples.

```{r min2-filter}
keep_proteins <- long_assigned %>%
  mutate(Detected = Intensity > 0) %>%
  group_by(Protein.Group, Age) %>%
  summarise(n_detected = sum(Detected, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Protein.Group) %>%
  summarise(keep = any(n_detected >= min_detect_n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(keep) %>%
  select(Protein.Group)

long_filt <- long_assigned %>%
  semi_join(keep_proteins, by = "Protein.Group")

cat("Assigned proteins before filter: ", n_distinct(long_assigned$Protein.Group), "\n", sep = "")

cat("Proteins after min2 filter: ", n_distinct(long_filt$Protein.Group), "\n", sep = "")

protein_counts_by_bin <- long_filt %>%
  distinct(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin) %>%
```

# Composition calculations

```{r composition-functions}
mass_composition_sample <- function(long_df, group_vars) {

  long_df %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(c(group_vars, "Sample")))) %>%
    mutate(total = sum(Intensity, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(c(group_vars, "Sample", "Bin")))) %>%
    summarise(Bin_intensity = sum(Intensity, na.rm = TRUE), total = dplyr::first(total), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(
      Fraction = if_else(total > 0, Bin_intensity / total, 0),
      Fraction_pct = Fraction * 100,
      Fraction_asin = asin(sqrt(Fraction))
    )
}

count_composition_sample <- function(long_df, group_vars) {

  sample_meta_local <- long_df %>%
    distinct(across(all_of(c(group_vars, "Sample"))))

  bins_local <- sort(unique(long_df$Bin))

  counts <- long_df %>%
    filter(Intensity > 0) %>%
    distinct(across(all_of(c(group_vars, "Sample", "Protein.Group", "Bin")))) %>%
    count(across(all_of(c(group_vars, "Sample", "Bin"))), name = "n_bin")

  complete_grid <- sample_meta_local %>%
    tidyr::crossing(Bin = bins_local)

  complete_grid %>%
    left_join(counts, by = c(group_vars, "Sample", "Bin")) %>%
    mutate(n_bin = replace_na(n_bin, 0L)) %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(c(group_vars, "Sample")))) %>%
    mutate(total_bin = sum(n_bin, na.rm = TRUE), Fraction = if_else(total_bin > 0, n_bin / total_bin, 0)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(Fraction_pct = Fraction * 100, Fraction_asin = asin(sqrt(Fraction)))
}

summarise_composition <- function(comp_df, group_vars) {

  comp_df %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(c(group_vars, "Bin")))) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_pct = mean(Fraction_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
      sem_pct = sd(Fraction_pct, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
      n = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

mass_sample_age <- mass_composition_sample(long_filt, "Age")

count_sample_age <- count_composition_sample(long_filt, "Age")

mass_sample_2x2 <- mass_composition_sample(long_filt, c("Age", "Sex"))

count_sample_2x2 <- count_composition_sample(long_filt, c("Age", "Sex"))

mass_overall <- summarise_composition(mass_sample_age, "Age")

count_overall <- summarise_composition(count_sample_age, "Age")

mass_2x2 <- summarise_composition(mass_sample_2x2, c("Age", "Sex"))

count_2x2 <- summarise_composition(count_sample_2x2, c("Age", "Sex"))

write.csv(mass_sample_age, file.path(comp_dir, "Mass_perSample_Age.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(count_sample_age, file.path(comp_dir, "Count_perSample_Age.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Descriptive composition summaries

These stacked summaries retain all assigned bins, including ER and Ribosome, because the purpose here is to describe the complete assigned composition.

```{r descriptive-composition, fig.keep="none"}

all_bins <- sort(unique(long_filt$Bin))

pal <- setNames(viridisLite::viridis(length(all_bins), option = "D", end = 0.95), all_bins)

# ── Overall Adult vs Old stacked plots ───────────────────────────────────────

make_stacked_plot <- function(df_plot, x_var, title, x_levels = NULL) {

  dd <- df_plot %>%
    mutate(Bin = as.character(Bin))

  if (!is.null(x_levels)) {
    dd[[x_var]] <- factor(dd[[x_var]], levels = x_levels)
  }

  bin_order <- dd %>%
    group_by(Bin) %>%
    summarise(contribution = sum(mean_pct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(contribution)) %>%
    pull(Bin)

  dd <- dd %>%
    mutate(Bin = factor(Bin, levels = bin_order))

  ggplot(dd, aes(x = .data[[x_var]], y = mean_pct, fill = Bin)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.70, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal, breaks = bin_order, drop = TRUE, name = "Cellular component") +
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = nm_fig3$full_composition_breaks_pct,
      limits = c(0, nm_fig3$full_composition_max_pct),
      labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
    ) +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = "Percent of assigned insoluble proteome") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
      legend.position = "right",
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    )
}

# ── Shared nested Age-within-Sex axis ────────────────────────────────────────
# Adult and Old are close together within each sex.
# Female and Male remain clearly separated.

age_sex_x <- tibble(
  Age = c("Adult", "Old", "Adult", "Old"),
  Sex = c("Female", "Female", "Male", "Male"),

  # Adult–Old gap = 0.40
  # Female–Male gap = 0.60
  x_pos = c(1.00, 1.40, 2.00, 2.40)
)

sex_axis_x <- tibble(

  x_start = c(0.85, 1.85),

# ── Nested Age × Sex stacked plot function ───────────────────────────────────

make_stacked_2x2_nested <- function(
  df_plot,
  title,
  y_label = "Percent of assigned insoluble proteome",
  full_proteome = FALSE
) {

  dd <- df_plot %>%
    mutate(Age = as.character(Age), Sex = as.character(Sex), Bin = as.character(Bin)) %>%
    left_join(age_sex_x, by = c("Age", "Sex"))

  bin_order <- dd %>%
    group_by(Bin) %>%
    summarise(contribution = sum(mean_pct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(contribution)) %>%
    pull(Bin)

  dd <- dd %>%
    mutate(Bin = factor(Bin, levels = bin_order))

  # Maximum stacked height.
  # For the complete composition plots this will be ~100%.
  # For the no-Sarco/Cyto plot it will be much smaller.
  y_max <- dd %>%
    group_by(Age, Sex) %>%
    summarise(group_total = sum(mean_pct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    summarise(y_max = max(group_total, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    pull(y_max)

  if (!is.finite(y_max) || y_max <= 0) {
    y_max <- 100
  }

  # Nested Sex annotations below Adult / Old
  sex_ann <- sex_axis_x %>%
    mutate(y_line = -0.095 * y_max, y_text = -0.17 * y_max)

  ggplot(dd, aes(x = x_pos, y = mean_pct, fill = Bin)) +

    # Thinner columns
    geom_col(width = 0.34, colour = "white", linewidth = nm_style$bar_outline) +

    # Horizontal line grouping Adult + Old within each sex
    geom_segment(
      data = sex_ann,
      aes(x = x_start, xend = x_end, y = y_line, yend = y_line),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      linewidth = nm_style$axis_line,
      colour = "grey35"
    ) +

    # Female / Male labels
    geom_text(
      data = sex_ann,
      aes(x = x_mid, y = y_text, label = Sex_label),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      size = nm_style$sex_group_font / ggplot2::.pt,
      fontface = "bold",
      colour = "grey25"
    ) +

    scale_fill_manual(values = pal, breaks = bin_order, drop = TRUE, name = "Cellular component") +

    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = age_sex_x$x_pos,
      labels = age_sex_x$Age,
      limits = c(0.65, 2.75),
      expand = expansion(mult = 0)
    ) +

    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = if (full_proteome) {
        nm_fig3$full_composition_breaks_pct
      } else {
        seq(0, floor(y_max * 1.045 / nm_fig3$noncontractile_tick_interval_pct) *
              nm_fig3$noncontractile_tick_interval_pct,
            by = nm_fig3$noncontractile_tick_interval_pct)
      },
      labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
    ) +

    coord_cartesian(
      ylim = c(0, if (full_proteome) nm_fig3$full_composition_max_pct else y_max * 1.045),
      clip = "off"
    ) +

    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = y_label) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +

    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),

      legend.position = "right",

      axis.text.x = element_text(size = nm_style$axis_text - 0.8, face = "plain", margin = margin(t = 1)),

      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),

      panel.grid = element_blank(),

      plot.margin = margin(t = 2, r = 1, b = 24, l = 5)
    )
}
```

# Bin-level statistics

## Statistical model

For each cellular-component bin, abundance-weighted per-sample fractions are arcsine-square-root transformed before inference.

The Age-only analysis uses:

`Fraction_asin ~ Age`

The factorial analysis uses:

`Fraction_asin ~ Age * Sex`

For the factorial model, Type III F tests with sum-to-zero contrasts are used so that the Age and Sex main effects are tested in the presence of the Age × Sex interaction. FDR is calculated separately across bins for Age, Sex, and Age × Sex.

```{r bin-statistics}
test_one_bin_age <- function(df_bin) {

  out <- tibble(p_Age = NA_real_)

  if (nrow(df_bin) < 4 || length(unique(df_bin$Fraction)) < 2) {
    return(out)
  }

  fit <- tryCatch(lm(Fraction_asin ~ Age, data = df_bin), error = function(e) NULL)

  if (is.null(fit)) {
    return(out)
  }

  an <- tryCatch(anova(fit), error = function(e) NULL)

  if (is.null(an)) {
    return(out)
  }

  tibble(
    p_Age = if ("Age" %in% rownames(an)) {
      an["Age", "Pr(>F)"]
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
  )
}

test_one_bin_2x2 <- function(df_bin) {

  out <- tibble(p_Age = NA_real_, p_Sex = NA_real_, p_AgeSex = NA_real_)

  if (nrow(df_bin) < 4 || length(unique(df_bin$Fraction)) < 2) {
    return(out)
  }

  dd <- df_bin %>%
    mutate(
      Age = droplevels(factor(Age, levels = c("Adult", "Old"))),
      Sex = droplevels(factor(Sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")))
    )

  if (nlevels(dd$Age) < 2 || nlevels(dd$Sex) < 2) {
    return(out)
  }

  contrasts(dd$Age) <- contr.sum(nlevels(dd$Age))

  contrasts(dd$Sex) <- contr.sum(nlevels(dd$Sex))

  fit <- tryCatch(lm(Fraction_asin ~ Age * Sex, data = dd), error = function(e) NULL)

  if (is.null(fit)) {
    return(out)
  }

  an <- tryCatch(car::Anova(fit, type = 3), error = function(e) NULL)

  if (is.null(an)) {
    return(out)
  }

  tibble(
    p_Age = if ("Age" %in% rownames(an)) {
      an["Age", "Pr(>F)"]
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },

    p_Sex = if ("Sex" %in% rownames(an)) {
      an["Sex", "Pr(>F)"]
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },

    p_AgeSex = if ("Age:Sex" %in% rownames(an)) {
      an["Age:Sex", "Pr(>F)"]
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
  )
}

run_bin_stats_age <- function(comp_df) {

  p_tbl <- comp_df %>%
    group_by(Bin) %>%
    group_modify(~ test_one_bin_age(.x)) %>%
    ungroup()

  means_tbl <- comp_df %>%
    group_by(Bin, Age) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_pct = mean(Fraction_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
      sem_pct = sd(Fraction_pct, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
      n = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Age, values_from = c(mean_pct, sem_pct, n)) %>%
    mutate(delta_old_minus_adult = mean_pct_Old - mean_pct_Adult)

  p_tbl %>%
    left_join(means_tbl, by = "Bin") %>%
    mutate(FDR_Age = p.adjust(p_Age, method = "BH")) %>%
    arrange(FDR_Age, desc(abs(delta_old_minus_adult)))
}

run_bin_stats_2x2 <- function(comp_df) {

  p_tbl <- comp_df %>%
    group_by(Bin) %>%
    group_modify(~ test_one_bin_2x2(.x)) %>%
    ungroup()

  means_group <- comp_df %>%
    mutate(Group = paste(Age, Sex, sep = "_")) %>%
    group_by(Bin, Group) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_pct = mean(Fraction_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
      sem_pct = sd(Fraction_pct, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
      n = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Group, values_from = c(mean_pct, sem_pct, n))

  means_age <- comp_df %>%
    group_by(Bin, Age) %>%
    summarise(mean_pct_age = mean(Fraction_pct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Age, values_from = mean_pct_age, names_prefix = "mean_pct_") %>%
    mutate(delta_old_minus_adult = mean_pct_Old - mean_pct_Adult)

  p_tbl %>%
    left_join(means_group, by = "Bin") %>%
    left_join(means_age, by = "Bin") %>%
    mutate(
      FDR_Age = p.adjust(p_Age, method = "BH"),
      FDR_Sex = p.adjust(p_Sex, method = "BH"),
      FDR_AgeSex = p.adjust(p_AgeSex, method = "BH")
    ) %>%
    arrange(FDR_Age, FDR_Sex, FDR_AgeSex)
}

mass_stats_age <- run_bin_stats_age(mass_sample_age)

mass_stats_2x2 <- run_bin_stats_2x2(mass_sample_2x2)

count_stats_age <- run_bin_stats_age(count_sample_age)

count_stats_2x2 <- run_bin_stats_2x2(count_sample_2x2)

write.csv(mass_stats_age, file.path(stats_dir, "BinStats_mass_Age.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(mass_stats_2x2, file.path(stats_split_dir, "BinStats_mass_2x2.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

This plot shows each sample, the group mean ± SEM, and both raw and FDR-adjusted p-values for Age, Sex, and the Age × Sex interaction. ER and Ribosome are omitted from this display.

```{r final-2x2-figure, fig.keep="none"}

p_bin_2x2 <- ggplot(plot_df_2x2, aes(x = x_pos, y = Fraction_pct)) +

  # Group means

  ) +

  # SEM
  stat_summary(

  ) +

  # Sex group names alone are sufficient at this size; the previous

  scale_x_continuous(

  # IMPORTANT:

  # for each cellular-component panel.
  facet_wrap(~ Bin_lab, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +

  # Do NOT specify ylim here.
  # That was what forced every panel to start at zero.
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +

  labs(
    title = "Insoluble proteome composition by cellular component",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Percent of total insoluble abundance",
    colour = "Age",
    shape = "Sex"
  ) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +

  theme(
    legend.position = "right",

    strip.text = ggtext::element_markdown(lineheight = 0.90, margin = margin(1.5, 1, 1.5, 1)),

    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = nm_style$axis_text, margin = margin(t = 5)),

    # Extra bottom room for Female/Male labels
    plot.margin = margin(t = 5, r = 5, b = 18, l = 5)
  )
```

# Summed raw insoluble abundance by cellular component

This section analyzes the **absolute summed raw insoluble abundance** assigned to each cellular-component bin. This is distinct from the abundance-weighted composition analysis above: the y-axis is the summed raw intensity in each bin rather than that bin's percentage of the total insoluble proteome.

For each mouse and cellular component, retained protein intensities are summed. Inferential tests are performed on `log2(summed raw abundance)` using the same 2 × 2 `Age × Sex` framework. The displayed raw-abundance panel shows the untransformed summed abundance, whereas the effect-size panel reports sex-specific **log2 fold changes (Old / Adult)** with 95% confidence intervals from the same log2-scale model.

```{r raw-bin-abundance-analysis, fig.keep="none"}
raw_bin_sample_2x2 <- long_filt %>%
  filter(Bin %in% bin_order_figure) %>%
  group_by(Sample, Age, Sex, Bin) %>%
  summarise(RawBinAbundance = sum(Intensity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    Age = factor(Age, levels = c("Adult", "Old")),
    Sex = factor(Sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    Bin = factor(as.character(Bin), levels = bin_order_figure),
    Group = factor(paste(Age, Sex, sep = "_"), levels = c("Adult_Female", "Old_Female", "Adult_Male", "Old_Male")),
    log2_RawBin = if_else(is.finite(RawBinAbundance) & RawBinAbundance > 0, log2(RawBinAbundance), NA_real_)
  )

run_rawbin_type3 <- function(data) {

  dd <- data %>%
    filter(is.finite(log2_RawBin)) %>%
    droplevels()

  if (nrow(dd) < 4 || nlevels(dd$Age) < 2 || nlevels(dd$Sex) < 2) {
    return(tibble(p_Age = NA_real_, p_Sex = NA_real_, p_AgeSex = NA_real_))
  }

  contrasts(dd$Age) <- contr.sum(nlevels(dd$Age))

  contrasts(dd$Sex) <- contr.sum(nlevels(dd$Sex))

  fit <- lm(log2_RawBin ~ Age * Sex, data = dd)

  a <- car::Anova(fit, type = 3)

  p_col <- grep("^Pr\\(", colnames(a), value = TRUE)[1]

  tibble(
    p_Age = if ("Age" %in% rownames(a)) {
      as.numeric(a["Age", p_col])
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    p_Sex = if ("Sex" %in% rownames(a)) {
      as.numeric(a["Sex", p_col])
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    p_AgeSex = if ("Age:Sex" %in% rownames(a)) {
      as.numeric(a["Age:Sex", p_col])
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
  )
}

run_rawbin_age_effects_by_sex <- function(data) {

  dd <- data %>%
    filter(is.finite(log2_RawBin)) %>%
    droplevels()

  if (nrow(dd) < 4 || nlevels(dd$Age) < 2 || nlevels(dd$Sex) < 2) {
    return(
      tibble(
        Sex = factor(character(), levels = c("Female", "Male")),
        log2FC = numeric(),
        SE = numeric(),
        df = numeric(),
        CI_low = numeric(),
        CI_high = numeric(),
        p_value = numeric()
      )
    )
  }

  contrasts(dd$Age) <- contr.sum(nlevels(dd$Age))

  contrasts(dd$Sex) <- contr.sum(nlevels(dd$Sex))

  fit <- lm(log2_RawBin ~ Age * Sex, data = dd)

  emm_age <- emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ Age | Sex)

  age_contrast <- emmeans::contrast(emm_age, method = "revpairwise", adjust = "none")

  as.data.frame(summary(age_contrast, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), adjust = "none")) %>%
    transmute(
      Sex = factor(as.character(Sex), levels = c("Female", "Male")),
      log2FC = estimate,
      SE = SE,
      df = df,
      CI_low = lower.CL,
      CI_high = upper.CL,
      p_value = p.value
    )
}

raw_bin_stats_2x2 <- raw_bin_sample_2x2 %>%
  group_by(Bin) %>%
  group_modify(~ run_rawbin_type3(.x)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    FDR_Age = p.adjust(p_Age, method = "BH"),
    FDR_Sex = p.adjust(p_Sex, method = "BH"),
    FDR_AgeSex = p.adjust(p_AgeSex, method = "BH")
  )

raw_bin_age_effects_by_sex <- raw_bin_sample_2x2 %>%
  group_by(Bin) %>%
  group_modify(~ run_rawbin_age_effects_by_sex(.x)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Bin = factor(as.character(Bin), levels = rev(bin_order_figure)))
```

# Effect-size analyses

Two effect-size definitions are retained because they answer different questions:

1. **Percentage-point effect:** Old − Adult in the percentage of the *total insoluble proteome* assigned to each bin.
2. **Within-bin relative change:** `100 × (Old − Adult) / Adult`, describing the relative change in that component's contribution compared with its Adult value.

Both pooled and sex-specific versions are exported.

```{r effect-size-data}
display_bins <- bin_order_figure[bin_order_figure %in% unique(mass_stats_age$Bin)]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bootstrap 95% CIs for the raw-scale descriptive effect sizes.
#
# Resampling is performed independently within Adult and Old for each
# cellular-component × Sex combination. This preserves the point-estimate
# definitions already used in the report:
#
#   percentage-point effect = mean(Old) - mean(Adult)
#   relative effect         = 100 * [mean(Old) - mean(Adult)] / mean(Adult)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
bootstrap_age_effect_ci <- function(
  data,
  value_col = "Fraction_pct",
  effect_type = c("difference", "relative"),
  n_boot = 5000
) {

  effect_type <- match.arg(effect_type)

  adult_values <- data[as.character(data$Age) == "Adult", value_col][[1]]

  old_values <- data[as.character(data$Age) == "Old", value_col][[1]]

  adult_values <- adult_values[is.finite(adult_values)]

  old_values <- old_values[is.finite(old_values)]

  if (length(adult_values) < 2 || length(old_values) < 2) {
    return(
      tibble(
        estimate_boot_reference = NA_real_,
        CI_low = NA_real_,
        CI_high = NA_real_,
        n_Adult = length(adult_values),
        n_Old = length(old_values)
      )
    )
  }

  adult_mean <- mean(adult_values)

  old_mean <- mean(old_values)

  estimate <- if (effect_type == "difference") {
    old_mean -
      adult_mean
  } else {
    if (adult_mean > 0) {
      100 *
        (old_mean - adult_mean) /
        adult_mean
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
  }

  boot_values <- replicate(
    n_boot,
    {

      adult_boot <- sample(adult_values, size = length(adult_values), replace = TRUE)

      old_boot <- sample(old_values, size = length(old_values), replace = TRUE)

      adult_boot_mean <- mean(adult_boot)

      old_boot_mean <- mean(old_boot)

      if (effect_type == "difference") {

        old_boot_mean -
          adult_boot_mean

      } else {

        if (adult_boot_mean > 0) {
          100 *
            (old_boot_mean - adult_boot_mean) /
            adult_boot_mean
        } else {
          NA_real_
        }
      }
    }
  )

  boot_values <- boot_values[is.finite(boot_values)]

  if (length(boot_values) < 100) {
    ci <- c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
  } else {
    ci <- as.numeric(quantile(boot_values, probs = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE, type = 7))
  }

  tibble(
    estimate_boot_reference = estimate,
    CI_low = ci[1],
    CI_high = ci[2],
    n_Adult = length(adult_values),
    n_Old = length(old_values)
  )
}

set.seed(20260909)

  filter(Bin %in% display_bins, !Bin %in% bins_to_remove_display) %>%
  group_by(Bin, Sex) %>%
  group_modify(
    ~ bootstrap_age_effect_ci(.x, value_col = "Fraction_pct", effect_type = "difference", n_boot = 5000)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

  filter(Bin %in% display_bins, !Bin %in% bins_to_remove_display) %>%
  group_by(Bin, Sex) %>%
  group_modify(
    ~ bootstrap_age_effect_ci(.x, value_col = "Fraction_pct", effect_type = "relative", n_boot = 5000)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

  filter(Bin %in% display_bins, !Bin %in% bins_to_remove_display) %>%
  mutate(Bin = factor(as.character(Bin), levels = rev(display_bins)))

effect_by_sex <- mass_stats_2x2 %>%
  filter(Bin %in% display_bins, !Bin %in% bins_to_remove_display) %>%
  mutate(
    delta_Female =
      mean_pct_Old_Female -
      mean_pct_Adult_Female,

    delta_Male =
      mean_pct_Old_Male -
      mean_pct_Adult_Male
  ) %>%
  select(Bin, p_Age, p_Sex, p_AgeSex, FDR_Age, FDR_Sex, FDR_AgeSex, delta_Female, delta_Male) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(delta_Female, delta_Male), names_to = "Sex", values_to = "delta_old_minus_adult") %>%
  mutate(Sex = dplyr::recode(Sex, delta_Female = "Female", delta_Male = "Male")) %>%

  )

within_by_sex <- mass_stats_2x2 %>%
  filter(Bin %in% display_bins, !Bin %in% bins_to_remove_display) %>%
  mutate(
    within_Female = if_else(
      !is.na(mean_pct_Adult_Female) &
        mean_pct_Adult_Female > 0,
      100 *
        (mean_pct_Old_Female - mean_pct_Adult_Female) /
        mean_pct_Adult_Female,
      NA_real_
    ),

    within_Male = if_else(
      !is.na(mean_pct_Adult_Male) &
        mean_pct_Adult_Male > 0,
      100 *
        (mean_pct_Old_Male - mean_pct_Adult_Male) /

    )

  select(Bin, p_Age, p_Sex, p_AgeSex, FDR_Age, FDR_Sex, FDR_AgeSex, within_Female, within_Male) %>%
```

```{r within-bin-effects, fig.keep="none"}
  scale_colour_manual(values = bin_colors_display, breaks = display_bins, drop = TRUE, guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = sex_shapes, name = "Sex") +
  add_minus10_xaxis(within_by_sex$withinbin_pct_change, within_by_sex$CI_low, within_by_sex$CI_high) +
  labs(
    title = "Relative age effect within each cellular component",
    subtitle = "Old vs Adult within each sex",
    x = "Within-component change (%)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  guides(shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(colour = "black", alpha = 1, size = nm_style$effect_point))) +
  effect_style_by_sex()
```

# Detection-frequency analysis

Detection is tested using a pooled two-sided Fisher's exact test comparing Adult and Old detection prevalence for each protein. BH FDR correction is then applied across the tested proteins.

The main reproducibility-filtered table uses the same `min2` protein set as the composition analysis. Exact Age-exclusive and relaxed Old-predominant subsets are exported separately.

```{r detection-analysis}
make_detection_table <- function(long_df) {

  long_df %>%
    group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Sample, Age, Sex) %>%
    summarise(Detected = as.integer(any(Intensity > 0, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop")
}

test_one_protein_detect <- function(df_prot) {

  adult_det <- sum(df_prot$Detected[df_prot$Age == "Adult"], na.rm = TRUE)

  adult_n <- sum(df_prot$Age == "Adult")

  old_det <- sum(df_prot$Detected[df_prot$Age == "Old"], na.rm = TRUE)

  old_n <- sum(df_prot$Age == "Old")

  fisher_mat <- matrix(c(adult_det, adult_n - adult_det, old_det, old_n - old_det), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)

  p_fisher <- tryCatch(fisher.test(fisher_mat)$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_)

  tibble(
    adult_detected_n = adult_det,
    adult_total_n = adult_n,
    old_detected_n = old_det,
    old_total_n = old_n,
    adult_prev = adult_det / adult_n,
    old_prev = old_det / old_n,
    delta_prev =
      old_det / old_n -
      adult_det / adult_n,
    p_detect_age_pooled = p_fisher
  )
}

run_detection_analysis <- function(long_df) {

  make_detection_table(long_df) %>%
    group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin) %>%
    group_modify(~ test_one_protein_detect(.x)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(
      FDR_detect_pooled = p.adjust(p_detect_age_pooled, method = "BH"),

      old_only_min2 =
        old_detected_n >= min_detect_n &
        adult_detected_n == 0,

      adult_only_min2 =
        adult_detected_n >= min_detect_n &
        old_detected_n == 0,

      old_predominant =
        old_detected_n >= min_detect_n &
        adult_detected_n <= 1
    ) %>%
    arrange(FDR_detect_pooled, desc(delta_prev))
}

detect_stats_all <- run_detection_analysis(long_assigned)

detect_stats_min2 <- run_detection_analysis(long_filt)

old_only_min2 <- detect_stats_min2 %>%
  filter(old_only_min2) %>%
  arrange(Bin, desc(old_detected_n), p_detect_age_pooled)

adult_only_min2 <- detect_stats_min2 %>%
  filter(adult_only_min2) %>%
  arrange(Bin, desc(adult_detected_n), p_detect_age_pooled)

old_predominant <- detect_stats_min2 %>%
  filter(old_predominant) %>%
  arrange(Bin, desc(old_detected_n), p_detect_age_pooled)

write.csv(detect_stats_all, file.path(detect_dir, "Detection_all.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(detect_stats_min2, file.path(detect_dir, "Detection_min2.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Top insoluble proteins by cellular component

The dot plot ranks proteins **within each cellular component by Old abundance** and displays those same proteins in Adult and Old. Only the eight final cellular-component panels are retained. Dot size represents log10 mean intensity.

```{r top10-dotplot, fig.keep="none"}
dot_df <- protein_bin_export %>%
  mutate(
    Status = case_when(
      !is.na(mean_intensity_Adult) &
        !is.na(mean_intensity_Old) ~ "Both",

      !is.na(mean_intensity_Adult) &
        is.na(mean_intensity_Old) ~ "Adult only",

      is.na(mean_intensity_Adult) &
        !is.na(mean_intensity_Old) ~ "Old only",

      TRUE ~ "Neither"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(Status != "Neither")

bins_all_dot <- sort(unique(dot_df$Bin))

bin_pal_dot <- setNames(viridisLite::viridis(length(bins_all_dot), option = "D", end = 0.95), bins_all_dot)

all_log10 <- log10(c(dot_df$mean_intensity_Adult, dot_df$mean_intensity_Old))

all_log10 <- all_log10[is.finite(all_log10)]

size_limits <- c(floor(min(all_log10)), ceiling(max(all_log10)))

size_breaks <- 4:7
size_breaks <- size_breaks[size_breaks >= size_limits[1] & size_breaks <= size_limits[2]]

if (length(size_breaks) == 0) {
  size_breaks <- pretty(size_limits, n = 4)
}

size_scale <- scale_size_continuous(
  name = expression(log[10](Intensity)),
  range = c(nm_style$dot_top10_min, nm_style$dot_top10_max),
  limits = size_limits,
  breaks = size_breaks,
  labels = paste0("10^", size_breaks),
  guide = guide_legend(order = 2, override.aes = list(colour = "grey30", alpha = 1))
)

dot_bin_order <- bin_order_figure[bin_order_figure %in% bins_all_dot]

color_scale_top10 <- scale_colour_manual(
  name = "Cellular component",
  values = bin_pal_dot,
  breaks = dot_bin_order,
  drop = FALSE,
  guide = guide_legend(order = 1, nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE, override.aes = list(size = 2.6, alpha = 1))
)

plot_list <- list()

for (i in seq_along(dot_bin_order)) {

  bin_name <- dot_bin_order[i]
  bin_col <- bin_pal_dot[[bin_name]]

  top10 <- dot_df %>%
    filter(Bin == bin_name, !is.na(mean_intensity_Old), mean_intensity_Old > 0) %>%
    arrange(desc(mean_intensity_Old)) %>%
    slice_head(n = 10)

  if (nrow(top10) == 0) {
    next
  }

  top10 <- top10 %>%
    mutate(GeneLabel = make.unique(as.character(Gene1)))

  plot_df <- top10 %>%
    select(GeneLabel, mean_intensity_Adult, mean_intensity_Old) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = c(mean_intensity_Adult, mean_intensity_Old),
      names_to = "Group",
      values_to = "Intensity"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Group = dplyr::recode(Group, mean_intensity_Adult = "Adult", mean_intensity_Old = "Old"),

      Group = factor(Group, levels = c("Adult", "Old")),

      log10_int = if_else(!is.na(Intensity) & Intensity > 0, log10(Intensity), NA_real_),

      GeneLabel = factor(GeneLabel, levels = rev(top10$GeneLabel)),

      Bin = factor(bin_name, levels = dot_bin_order)
    )

  p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Group, y = GeneLabel, size = log10_int, colour = Bin)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.90, na.rm = TRUE, show.legend = TRUE) +
    size_scale +
    color_scale_top10 +
    scale_x_discrete(position = "top", labels = c("Adult" = "Adult", "Old" = "Old")) +
    labs(title = bin_name, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = nm_style$dot_protein_title_pt, colour = bin_col),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = nm_style$dot_group_label_pt, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = nm_style$dot_protein_label_pt),
      axis.line = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey93", linewidth = 0.3),
      legend.position = if (i == 1) {
        "bottom"
      } else {
        "none"
      },
      plot.margin = margin(2, 3, 2, 3)
    )

  plot_list[[bin_name]] <- p
}

combined_dotplot <- patchwork::wrap_plots(plotlist = plot_list, ncol = 4) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Most abundant insoluble proteins by cellular component",
    subtitle = "Top 10 proteins in each component ranked by Old abundance",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8.0, hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 6.0, colour = "grey35", hjust = 0.5)
    )
  ) &
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 5.5),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 4.8)
  )

dotplot_png <- file.path(dot_dir, "Top10_AllBins.png")

save_plot_png(combined_dotplot, dotplot_png, width = 11.5, height = 6.5, dpi = 300)
```

# Sex-resolved protein abundance summaries

For each retained protein, abundance is summarized separately within Adult Female, Old Female, Adult Male, and Old Male groups. Mean and median intensity are calculated **only among samples with positive detected intensity**; non-detections are not entered as zero-valued abundance observations in these summaries.

Detection counts are exported alongside the abundance values so low-prevalence means can be recognized. Detection prevalence is calculated as the number of samples with positive intensity divided by the total number of samples in that Age × Sex group. Both long- and wide-format tables are exported for downstream inspection.

```{r abundance-summary}
# ── Mean abundance among detected samples ─────────────────────────────────────
abundance_by_sex <- long_filt %>%
  filter(Intensity > 0) %>%
  group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Sex, Age) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_intensity =
      mean(Intensity, na.rm = TRUE),

    median_intensity =
      median(Intensity, na.rm = TRUE),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ── Detection n / total for context ───────────────────────────────────────────
detection_by_sex_for_abundance <- long_filt %>%
  group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Sex, Age, Sample) %>%
  summarise(Detected = as.integer(any(Intensity > 0, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Sex, Age) %>%
  summarise(
    detected_n =
      sum(Detected, na.rm = TRUE),

    total_n =
      n(),

    prevalence =
      detected_n /
      total_n,

    .groups = "drop"
  )

abundance_by_sex_export <- abundance_by_sex %>%
  full_join(detection_by_sex_for_abundance, by = c("Protein.Group", "Gene1", "Bin", "Sex", "Age")) %>%
  arrange(factor(Bin, levels = bin_priority), Sex, Age, desc(mean_intensity))

write.csv(abundance_by_sex_export, file.path(split_dot_dir, "Protein_abundance_bySex_long.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Wide table useful for inspection
abundance_by_sex_wide <- abundance_by_sex_export %>%
  mutate(Group = paste(Age, Sex, sep = "_")) %>%
  select(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Group, mean_intensity, median_intensity, detected_n, total_n, prevalence) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Group,
    values_from = c(mean_intensity, median_intensity, detected_n, total_n, prevalence)
  )

write.csv(abundance_by_sex_wide, file.path(split_dot_dir, "Protein_abundance_bySex_wide.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```
# Shared pooled-abundance table for sex-resolved Top-10 displays

The pooled Adult/Old protein-abundance table created above is reused for the sex-resolved Top-10 displays. No second abundance calculation or GO assignment is performed.

```{r pooled-top10-support}
protein_bin_pooled <- protein_bin_export

# The cellular-component palette and display order were created in the
# combined Top-10 section and are reused below.
```
# Pooled Old-ranked Top 10 resolved into four Age × Sex groups

Within each displayed cellular component, proteins are ranked by **pooled Old mean abundance** and the ten most abundant proteins are selected. Those same proteins are then displayed in four groups—Adult Female, Old Female, Adult Male, and Old Male—so that sex-resolved abundance patterns can be evaluated without changing the protein set between groups.

```{r pooled-top10-bysex-data}
pooled_top10 <- protein_bin_pooled %>%
  filter(Bin %in% dot_bin_order, !is.na(mean_intensity_Old), mean_intensity_Old > 0) %>%
  group_by(Bin) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_intensity_Old), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, pooled_Old_mean = mean_intensity_Old)

pooled_top10_bysex <- pooled_top10 %>%
  left_join(abundance_by_sex_export, by = c("Protein.Group", "Gene1", "Bin")) %>%
  mutate(
    Group = paste(Age, Sex, sep = "_"),

    Group = factor(Group, levels = c("Adult_Female", "Old_Female", "Adult_Male", "Old_Male"))
  )

write.csv(pooled_top10_bysex, file.path(split_dot_dir, "Top10_PooledOldRank_bySex_table.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r pooled-top10-bysex-plot, fig.keep="none"}
plot_list_4groups <- list()

    left_join(rank_tbl %>% select(Protein.Group, GeneLabel), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
    mutate(
      log10_int =
        if_else(!is.na(mean_intensity) & mean_intensity > 0, log10(mean_intensity), NA_real_),

      GeneLabel = factor(GeneLabel, levels = rev(rank_tbl$GeneLabel))
    )

  if (nrow(plot_df) == 0) {
    next
  }

  p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Group, y = GeneLabel, size = log10_int, colour = Bin)) +

    geom_point(alpha = 0.90, na.rm = TRUE, show.legend = TRUE) +

    size_scale_sex +
    color_scale_top10_sex +

    scale_x_discrete(
      position = "top",
      labels = c(
        "Adult_Female" =
          "Adult\nF",
        "Old_Female" =
          "Old\nF",
        "Adult_Male" =
          "Adult\nM",
        "Old_Male" =
          "Old\nM"
      )
    ) +

    labs(title = bin_name, x = NULL, y = NULL) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +

    theme(
      plot.title =
        element_text(face = "bold", size = nm_style$dot_protein_title_pt, colour = bin_col),

      axis.text.x =
        element_text(size = nm_style$dot_group_label_pt, face = "bold"),

      axis.text.y =
        element_text(size = nm_style$dot_protein_label_pt),

      axis.line =
        element_blank(),

      axis.ticks =
        element_blank(),

      panel.grid.major =
        element_line(colour = "grey93", linewidth = 0.12),

      legend.position =
        if (i == 1) {
          "bottom"
        } else {
          "none"
        },

      plot.margin =
        margin(1, 1, 1, 1)
    )

  plot_list_4groups[[bin_name]] <- p
}
```

# Sex-specific Top-10 rankings

The pooled Old-ranked display above fixes one common protein set for comparison across all four groups. The sex-specific rankings answer a different compositional question: **which proteins are most abundant within each cellular component in Old Female muscle, and which are most abundant in Old Male muscle?**

Female and Male rankings are therefore generated independently. Within each sex and cellular component, proteins are ordered by mean positive intensity in Old mice, the ten most abundant are selected, and the corresponding Adult abundance for those same proteins is displayed. The membership-overlap analysis in the next section identifies proteins shared between the Female and Male Top-10 lists and proteins appearing in only one sex-specific list.

```{r sex-specific-top10-function}
make_sex_top10 <- function(sex_name, abundance_tbl, bins_order, palette) {

  sex_tbl <- abundance_tbl %>%
    filter(Sex == sex_name)

  rank_tbl <- sex_tbl %>%
    filter(Age == "Old", !is.na(mean_intensity), mean_intensity > 0, Bin %in% bins_order) %>%
    group_by(Bin) %>%
    arrange(desc(mean_intensity), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    slice_head(n = 10) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    transmute(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Old_rank_mean = mean_intensity)

  plot_tbl <- rank_tbl %>%
    left_join(sex_tbl, by = c("Protein.Group", "Gene1", "Bin"))

  write.csv(
    plot_tbl,
    file.path(split_dot_dir, paste0("Top10_", sex_name, "_OldRank_table.csv")),
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  logvals <- log10(plot_tbl$mean_intensity)

  logvals <- logvals[is.finite(logvals)]

  if (length(logvals) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  lims <- c(floor(min(logvals)), ceiling(max(logvals)))

  brks <- 4:7

  brks <- brks[brks >= lims[1] & brks <= lims[2]]

  if (length(brks) == 0) {
    brks <- pretty(lims, n = 4)
  }

  this_size_scale <-
    scale_size_continuous(
      name =
        expression(log[10](Intensity)),
      range = c(2.5, 7),
      limits = lims,
      breaks = brks,
      labels = paste0("10^", brks),
      guide =
        guide_legend(override.aes = list(colour = "grey30", alpha = 1))
    )

  plot_list <- list()

  for (i in seq_along(bins_order)) {

    bin_name <-
      bins_order[i]

    bin_col <-
      palette[[bin_name]]

    rank_bin <- rank_tbl %>%
      filter(Bin == bin_name) %>%
      arrange(desc(Old_rank_mean)) %>%
      mutate(GeneLabel = make.unique(as.character(Gene1)))

    if (nrow(rank_bin) == 0) {
      next
    }

    plot_df <- plot_tbl %>%
      filter(Bin == bin_name) %>%
      left_join(rank_bin %>% select(Protein.Group, GeneLabel), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
      mutate(
        Age = factor(Age, levels = c("Adult", "Old")),

        log10_int =
          if_else(!is.na(mean_intensity) & mean_intensity > 0, log10(mean_intensity), NA_real_),

        GeneLabel =
          factor(GeneLabel, levels = rev(rank_bin$GeneLabel))
      )

    p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Age, y = GeneLabel, size = log10_int)) +

      geom_point(colour = bin_col, alpha = 0.90, na.rm = TRUE, show.legend = i == 1) +

      this_size_scale +

      scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +

      labs(title = bin_name, x = NULL, y = NULL) +

      theme_classic(base_size = 12) +

      theme(
        plot.title =
          element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, colour = bin_col),

        axis.text.x =
          element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),

        axis.text.y =
          element_text(size = 9),

        axis.line =
          element_blank(),

        axis.ticks =
          element_blank(),

        panel.grid.major =
          element_line(colour = "grey93", linewidth = 0.3),

        legend.position =
          if (i == 1) {
            "right"
          } else {
            "none"
          },

        plot.margin =
          margin(6, 10, 6, 10)
      )

    plot_list[[bin_name]] <- p
  }

  combined <-
    patchwork::wrap_plots(plotlist = plot_list, ncol = 4) +

    patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") +

    patchwork::plot_annotation(
      title =
        paste0("Most abundant insoluble proteins — ", sex_name),

      subtitle =
        paste0("Top 10 proteins in each component ranked by Old ", sex_name, " abundance"),

      theme =
        theme(
          plot.title =
            element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),

          plot.subtitle =
            element_text(size = 11, colour = "grey35", hjust = 0.5)
        )
    ) &

    theme(legend.position = "right")

  out_png <- file.path(split_dot_dir, paste0("Top10_", sex_name, "_OldRank.png"))

  save_plot_png(combined, out_png, width = 11.5, height = 6.5, dpi = 300)

  list(ranking = rank_tbl, data = plot_tbl, plot = combined, png = out_png)
}
```

# Compare Female and Male Old Top-10 membership

This table identifies whether each Old-ranked Top-10 protein appears in the Female list, Male list, or both.

```{r top10-membership-overlap}
female_membership <-
  if (!is.null(female_top10)) {
    female_top10$ranking %>%
      transmute(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Female_Top10 = TRUE)
  } else {
    tibble(Protein.Group = character(), Gene1 = character(), Bin = character(), Female_Top10 = logical())
  }

male_membership <-
  if (!is.null(male_top10)) {
    male_top10$ranking %>%
      transmute(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Male_Top10 = TRUE)
  } else {
    tibble(Protein.Group = character(), Gene1 = character(), Bin = character(), Male_Top10 = logical())
  }

top10_overlap <- full_join(female_membership, male_membership, by = c("Protein.Group", "Gene1", "Bin")) %>%
  mutate(
    Female_Top10 =
      replace_na(Female_Top10, FALSE),

    Male_Top10 =
      replace_na(Male_Top10, FALSE),

    Membership =
      case_when(
        Female_Top10 &
          Male_Top10 ~
          "Both",

        Female_Top10 &
          !Male_Top10 ~
          "Female only",

        !Female_Top10 &
          Male_Top10 ~
          "Male only",

        TRUE ~
          "Neither"
      )
  ) %>%
  arrange(factor(Bin, levels = bin_order_figure), Membership, Gene1)

write.csv(top10_overlap, file.path(split_dot_dir, "Top10_FemaleMale_membership_overlap.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Sex-specific detection-frequency analysis

The detection analysis is run independently within Female and Male mice and treats detection as a binary outcome (`Intensity > 0`) rather than as a continuous abundance value.

For each protein and sex:

- Adult detection prevalence is calculated only from Adult samples of that sex.
- Old detection prevalence is calculated only from Old samples of that sex.
- A 2 × 2 table of Age (`Adult`, `Old`) by detection status (`detected`, `not detected`) is evaluated with a two-sided Fisher's exact test.
- The prevalence difference is calculated as `Old prevalence − Adult prevalence`.
- Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction is applied separately across the Female protein tests and across the Male protein tests.

Two protein universes are exported:

1. **All GO-assigned proteins:** useful for complete prevalence inspection.
2. **Sex-specific min2 universe:** proteins detected in at least 2 Adult samples **or** at least 2 Old samples within that sex.

The sex-specific min2 universe is used for reproducible detection categories:

- `old_only`: Old detected ≥2 and Adult detected =0.
- `adult_only`: Adult detected ≥2 and Old detected =0.
- `old_predominant`: Old detected ≥2 and Adult detected ≤1.

These categories are descriptive filters. Fisher p-values quantify within-sex Adult-versus-Old detection differences, while BH-FDR values provide multiplicity-adjusted inference.

```{r sex-specific-detection-functions}
make_detection_table_sex <- function(long_df) {

  long_df %>%
    group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Sex, Sample, Age) %>%
    summarise(Detected = as.integer(any(Intensity > 0, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop")
}

test_one_protein_detect_sex <- function(df_prot) {

  adult_det <- sum(df_prot$Detected[df_prot$Age == "Adult"], na.rm = TRUE)

  adult_n <- sum(df_prot$Age == "Adult")

  old_det <- sum(df_prot$Detected[df_prot$Age == "Old"], na.rm = TRUE)

  old_n <- sum(df_prot$Age == "Old")

  if (adult_n == 0 || old_n == 0) {

    return(
      tibble(
        adult_detected_n =
          adult_det,
        adult_total_n =
          adult_n,
        old_detected_n =
          old_det,
        old_total_n =
          old_n,
        adult_prev =
          NA_real_,
        old_prev =
          NA_real_,
        delta_prev =
          NA_real_,
        p_detect_age =
          NA_real_
      )
    )
  }

  fisher_mat <- matrix(c(adult_det, adult_n - adult_det, old_det, old_n - old_det), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)

  p_fisher <- tryCatch(fisher.test(fisher_mat, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_)

  tibble(
    adult_detected_n =
      adult_det,

    adult_total_n =
      adult_n,

    old_detected_n =
      old_det,

    old_total_n =
      old_n,

    adult_prev =
      adult_det /
      adult_n,

    old_prev =
      old_det /
      old_n,

    delta_prev =
      old_det /
      old_n -
      adult_det /
      adult_n,

    p_detect_age =
      p_fisher
  )
}

run_detection_by_sex <- function(long_df, apply_sex_min2 = FALSE) {

  det_long <-
    make_detection_table_sex(long_df)

  det_stats <- det_long %>%
    group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Sex) %>%
    group_modify(~ test_one_protein_detect_sex(.x)) %>%
    ungroup()

  if (apply_sex_min2) {

    det_stats <- det_stats %>%
      filter(adult_detected_n >= min_detect_n | old_detected_n >= min_detect_n)
  }

  det_stats %>%
    group_by(Sex) %>%
    mutate(
      FDR_detect =
        p.adjust(p_detect_age, method = "BH"),

      old_only =
        old_detected_n >=
          min_detect_n &
        adult_detected_n == 0,

      adult_only =
        adult_detected_n >=
          min_detect_n &
        old_detected_n == 0,

      old_predominant =
        old_detected_n >=
          min_detect_n &
        adult_detected_n <= 1
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    arrange(Sex, FDR_detect, desc(delta_prev))
}
```

# Sex-specific Old-predominant detection plots

These plots display proteins meeting the relaxed Old-predominant criterion within each sex (`Old detected ≥2`, `Adult detected ≤1`).

A filled colored dot marks Old detection, a hollow colored Adult dot marks a singleton Adult detection, and a grey X marks complete Adult absence. The fraction printed beside the Old dot is the number of Old samples with detection divided by the total number of Old samples of that sex. The displayed p-value is the **within-sex two-sided Adult-versus-Old Fisher test**; BH-FDR values are retained in the exported table.

```{r detection-plot-function}
make_old_predominant_sex_plot <- function(sex_name, detect_tbl, long_df, palette) {

  sex_det <- detect_tbl %>%
    filter(Sex == sex_name, old_predominant)

  if (nrow(sex_det) == 0) {

    message("No Old-predominant proteins for ", sex_name, " using Old >= ", min_detect_n, " and Adult <= 1.")

    return(NULL)
  }

  # Mean detected abundance, used only for ordering context/export.
  sex_mean <- long_df %>%
    filter(Sex == sex_name, Intensity > 0) %>%
    group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Age) %>%
    summarise(mean_intensity = mean(Intensity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Age, values_from = mean_intensity, names_prefix = "mean_intensity_")

  plot_df <- sex_det %>%
    left_join(sex_mean, by = c("Protein.Group", "Gene1", "Bin")) %>%
    mutate(
      adult_absent =
        adult_detected_n == 0,

      adult_singleton =
        adult_detected_n == 1,

      adult_prev_label =
        sprintf("%d/%d", adult_detected_n, adult_total_n),

      old_prev_label =
        sprintf("%d/%d", old_detected_n, old_total_n),

      p_label =
        fmt_p_detection(p_detect_age),

      p_fontface =
        if_else(!is.na(p_detect_age) & p_detect_age <= 0.050, "bold", "plain"),

      Gene1_label =
        if_else(!is.na(p_detect_age) & p_detect_age <= 0.050, paste0("**", Gene1, "**"), Gene1)
    ) %>%
    arrange(factor(Bin, levels = bin_priority), desc(old_detected_n), desc(mean_intensity_Old), Gene1)

  used_bins <- bin_priority[bin_priority %in% unique(plot_df$Bin)]

  plot_df <- plot_df %>%
    mutate(Gene1 = factor(Gene1, levels = rev(unique(Gene1))), Bin = factor(Bin, levels = used_bins))

  gene_label_map <-
    stats::setNames(plot_df$Gene1_label, as.character(plot_df$Gene1))

  adult_x <- 1.00
  old_x   <- 1.60
  p_x     <- 2.02

  row_guides <- tibble(Gene1 = levels(plot_df$Gene1))

  p <- ggplot() +

    geom_segment(
      data =
        row_guides,
      aes(x = 0.72, xend = 1.84, y = Gene1, yend = Gene1),
      colour = "grey92",
      linewidth = 0.35
    ) +

    geom_vline(xintercept = c(adult_x, old_x), colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.35) +

    # Adult absent
    geom_point(
      data =
        plot_df %>%
        filter(adult_absent),
      aes(x = adult_x, y = Gene1),
      shape = 4,
      size = nm_style$oldpred_adult_symbol_mm,
      colour = "grey70",
      stroke = nm_style$oldpred_adult_stroke_mm
    ) +

    # Adult singleton
    geom_point(
      data =
        plot_df %>%
        filter(adult_singleton),
      aes(x = adult_x, y = Gene1, colour = Bin),
      shape = 1,
      size = nm_style$oldpred_adult_symbol_mm,
      stroke = nm_style$oldpred_adult_stroke_mm
    ) +

    # Robust Old detection
    geom_point(
      data =
        plot_df,
      aes(x = old_x, y = Gene1, colour = Bin),
      shape = 16,
      size = nm_style$oldpred_old_symbol_mm
    ) +

    # Old prevalence
    geom_text(
      data =
        plot_df,
      aes(x = old_x, y = Gene1, label = old_prev_label),
      nudge_x = 0.10,
      hjust = 0,
      size = nm_style$oldpred_old_prevalence_text_mm,
      colour = "grey25"
    ) +

    # Fisher p-value
    geom_text(
      data =
        plot_df,
      aes(x = p_x, y = Gene1, label = p_label, fontface = p_fontface),
      hjust = 0,
      size = nm_style$oldpred_fisher_text_mm,
      colour = "grey40",
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +

    scale_colour_manual(
      values =
        palette[used_bins],
      breaks =
        used_bins,
      drop = TRUE,
      name =
        "Cellular component"
    ) +

    scale_y_discrete(labels = gene_label_map) +

    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = c(adult_x, old_x, p_x),
      labels = c("Adult", "Old", ""),
      position = "top",
      expand =
        expansion(add = c(0, 0.58))
    ) +

    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +

    labs(
      title = NULL,
      subtitle = NULL,

      caption =
        paste0(
          "Filled dot = Old detected (>=2); ",
          "hollow dot = Adult singleton; grey X = Adult absent.\n",
          "* denotes within-sex Fisher p <= 0.05; ",
          "BH FDR values are exported in the accompanying table."
        ),

      x = NULL,
      y = NULL
    ) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +

    theme(
      plot.title =
        element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),

      plot.subtitle =
        element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 10.5),

      plot.caption =
        element_text(colour = "grey45", size = 8, hjust = 0),

      plot.caption.position =
        "plot",

      axis.text.y =
        ggtext::element_markdown(size = 9.5),

      axis.line =
        element_blank(),

      axis.ticks =
        element_blank(),

      panel.grid =
        element_blank(),

      legend.position =
        "right",

      plot.margin =
        margin(10, 15, 15, 10)
    )

  out_png <- file.path(split_detect_dir, paste0("OldPredominant_", sex_name, ".png"))

  out_csv <- file.path(split_detect_dir, paste0("OldPredominant_", sex_name, "_table.csv"))

  save_plot_png(p, out_png, width = 6.4, height = max(5, nrow(plot_df) * 0.30 + 2.3), dpi = 300)

  write.csv(plot_df, out_csv, row.names = FALSE)

  list(data = plot_df, plot = p, png = out_png, csv = out_csv)
}
```

# Female-versus-Male overlap of Old-predominant proteins

This comparison joins the Female and Male Old-predominant lists by `Protein.Group`, gene, and GO-CC bin and classifies each protein as `Both sexes`, `Female only`, or `Male only`.

This classification describes whether a protein crosses the predefined detection criterion in each sex. It is **not** a statistical test comparing Female and Male detection responses. A protein classified as `Female only` or `Male only` can arise because of small differences in prevalence or sample size; a formal sex difference would require an explicit interaction model for detection.

```{r detection-sex-overlap}
female_oldpred <- old_predominant_bysex %>%
  filter(Sex == "Female") %>%
  transmute(
    Protein.Group,
    Gene1,
    Bin,
    Female_old_predominant =
      TRUE,
    Female_Adult_n =
      adult_detected_n,
    Female_Adult_total =
      adult_total_n,
    Female_Old_n =
      old_detected_n,
    Female_Old_total =
      old_total_n,
    Female_delta_prev =
      delta_prev,
    Female_p =
      p_detect_age,
    Female_FDR =
      FDR_detect
  )

male_oldpred <- old_predominant_bysex %>%
  filter(Sex == "Male") %>%
  transmute(
    Protein.Group,
    Gene1,
    Bin,
    Male_old_predominant =
      TRUE,
    Male_Adult_n =
      adult_detected_n,
    Male_Adult_total =
      adult_total_n,
    Male_Old_n =
      old_detected_n,
    Male_Old_total =
      old_total_n,
    Male_delta_prev =
      delta_prev,
    Male_p =
      p_detect_age,
    Male_FDR =
      FDR_detect
  )

oldpred_overlap <- full_join(female_oldpred, male_oldpred, by = c("Protein.Group", "Gene1", "Bin")) %>%
  mutate(
    Female_old_predominant =
      replace_na(Female_old_predominant, FALSE),

    Male_old_predominant =
      replace_na(Male_old_predominant, FALSE),

    Detection_pattern =
      case_when(
        Female_old_predominant &
          Male_old_predominant ~
          "Both sexes",

        Female_old_predominant &
          !Male_old_predominant ~
          "Female only",

        !Female_old_predominant &
          Male_old_predominant ~
          "Male only",

        TRUE ~
          "Neither"
      )
  ) %>%
  arrange(factor(Bin, levels = bin_order_figure), Detection_pattern, Gene1)

write.csv(oldpred_overlap, file.path(split_detect_dir, "OldPredominant_FemaleMale_overlap.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

oldpred_overlap_summary <- oldpred_overlap %>%
  count(Detection_pattern, name = "n_proteins")

write.csv(
  oldpred_overlap_summary,
  file.path(split_detect_dir, "OldPredominant_FemaleMale_overlap_summary.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

oldpred_overlap_summary
```

## Alternative manuscript-ready detection visualizations

The complete Female and Male Old-predominant protein plots above are retained. The following additional visualizations provide more compact views of the same sex-resolved detection results.

They answer four complementary questions:

1. **Component-level summary:** Which cellular components contribute most to the Old-predominant detection pattern in Female and Male mice?
2. **Female-versus-Male detection-change scatter:** How do the age-associated detection changes compare between sexes for proteins appearing in either sex-specific Old-predominant list?
3. **Protein-wise delta view:** What is the magnitude of the Old-versus-Adult detection change for each Old-predominant protein in the sex(es) in which it meets the criterion?
4. **Selected-candidate four-group matrix:** What are the actual Adult Female, Old Female, Adult Male, and Old Male detection prevalences for the strongest candidates?

These analyses are descriptive/exploratory. In particular, distance from the diagonal in the Female-versus-Male detection scatter is **not** a formal statistical Age × Sex interaction test for binary detection.

### Component-level summary of Old-predominant proteins

The count panel shows the number of proteins meeting the sex-specific relaxed Old-predominant criterion:

- Old detected in at least 2 samples within that sex
- Adult detected in no more than 1 sample within that sex

Because cellular components contain different numbers of testable proteins, a second panel expresses the same result as the percentage of sex-specific `min2` proteins within each component.

```{r detection-component-summary, fig.keep="none"}
sex_detection_cols <- c("Female" = "#CC66B4", "Male"   = "#00A087")

component_detection_summary <- detect_bysex_min2 %>%
  filter(Bin %in% bin_order_figure) %>%
  mutate(Sex = as.character(Sex), Bin = as.character(Bin)) %>%
  group_by(Sex, Bin) %>%
  summarise(n_tested = n(), n_oldpred = sum(old_predominant, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::complete(Sex = c("Female", "Male"), Bin = bin_order_figure, fill = list(n_tested = 0, n_oldpred = 0)) %>%
  mutate(
    prop_oldpred = if_else(n_tested > 0, n_oldpred / n_tested, NA_real_),

    Sex = factor(Sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),

    Bin = factor(Bin, levels = rev(bin_order_figure))
  )

write.csv(
  component_detection_summary,
  file.path(split_detect_dir, "OldPredominant_ComponentSummary_bySex.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

p_detection_component_count <- ggplot(component_detection_summary, aes(x = n_oldpred, y = Bin, fill = Sex)) +

  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.76), width = 0.3) +

  geom_text(aes(label = n_oldpred), position = position_dodge(width = 0.76), hjust = -0.20, size = 2.0) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = sex_detection_cols) +

  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14))) +

  labs(
    title =
      "Old-predominant proteins by cellular component",

    subtitle =
      "Number meeting Old >= 2 and Adult <= 1 within each sex",

    x =
      "Number of Old-predominant proteins",

    y = NULL,

    fill = "Sex"
  ) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    plot.title =
      element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),

    plot.subtitle =
      element_text(colour = "grey35", size = 9.5),

    legend.position =
      "top",

    axis.text.y =
      element_text(size = 9.5)
  )

p_detection_component_prop <- ggplot(component_detection_summary, aes(x = prop_oldpred, y = Bin, fill = Sex)) +

  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.76), width = 0.3, na.rm = TRUE) +

  geom_text(
    data =
      component_detection_summary %>%
      filter(!is.na(prop_oldpred)),
    aes(label = scales::percent(prop_oldpred, accuracy = 1)),
    position =
      position_dodge(width = 0.76),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 3.0
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = sex_detection_cols) +

  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +

  labs(
    title =
      "Old-predominant proteins as a proportion of testable proteins",

    subtitle =
      "Denominator = sex-specific min2 proteins within each component",

    x =
      "Old-predominant proteins / testable proteins",

    y = NULL,

    fill = "Sex"
  ) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    plot.title =
      element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),

    plot.subtitle =
      element_text(colour = "grey35", size = 9.5),

    legend.position =
      "top",

    axis.text.y =
      element_text(size = 9.5)
  )

p_detection_component_combined <-
  p_detection_component_count +
  p_detection_component_prop +

  patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") &

  theme(legend.position = "top")

component_count_png <- file.path(split_detect_dir, "OldPredominant_ComponentSummary_Count.png")

component_prop_png <- file.path(split_detect_dir, "OldPredominant_ComponentSummary_Percent.png")

component_combined_png <- file.path(split_detect_dir, "OldPredominant_ComponentSummary_CountAndPercent.png")

save_plot_png(p_detection_component_count, component_count_png, width = 7.0, height = 5.2, dpi = 300)

save_plot_png(p_detection_component_prop, component_prop_png, width = 7.0, height = 5.2, dpi = 300)
```
