### Female-versus-Male change in detection prevalence

This plot is the detection analogue of the Female-versus-Male age-effect abundance scatter.

For each protein:

- **x-axis:** Female change in prevalence = Old Female prevalence − Adult Female prevalence
- **y-axis:** Male change in prevalence = Old Male prevalence − Adult Male prevalence
- dotted `y = x` = identical prevalence change in Female and Male mice
- upper-right = detection increases with age in both sexes
- lower-left = detection decreases with age in both sexes
- lower-right = detection increases in Female mice but decreases in Male mice
- upper-left = detection decreases in Female mice but increases in Male mice

The delta figure is restricted to the **union of proteins meeting the relaxed Old-predominant criterion in Female or Male mice**, so the proteins shown correspond directly to the complete sex-specific lists above. The x-coordinate is `Old Female prevalence − Adult Female prevalence`; the y-coordinate is `Old Male prevalence − Adult Male prevalence`.

A **circle** denotes a Female Old-predominant result and a **triangle** denotes a Male Old-predominant result. Open symbols indicate a nonsignificant within-sex Fisher test, whereas filled symbols indicate raw `p ≤ 0.05`. A sex-specific symbol is drawn only when that protein meets the Old-predominant criterion in that sex. Cellular-component identity is encoded by color. Small deterministic visual offsets are used only to separate proteins with identical prevalence-change coordinates; the underlying delta values are unchanged. Distance from `y = x` remains descriptive and is not a formal Age × Sex interaction test.

```{r detection-female-male-scatter-data}
detect_comparison_long <- detect_bysex_all %>%
  filter(Bin %in% dot_bin_order) %>%
  group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin) %>%
  filter(any(adult_detected_n >= min_detect_n | old_detected_n >= min_detect_n)) %>%
  ungroup()

detect_female_male <- detect_comparison_long %>%
  select(
    Protein.Group,
    Gene1,
    Bin,
    Sex,
    adult_detected_n,
    adult_total_n,
    adult_prev,
    old_detected_n,
    old_total_n,
    old_prev,
    delta_prev,
    p_detect_age,
    FDR_detect,
    old_only,
    old_predominant
  ) %>%
  mutate(Sex = as.character(Sex)) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from =
      Sex,

    values_from = c(
      adult_detected_n,
      adult_total_n,
      adult_prev,
      old_detected_n,
      old_total_n,
      old_prev,
      delta_prev,
      p_detect_age,
      FDR_detect,
      old_only,
      old_predominant
    ),

    names_glue =
      "{.value}_{Sex}"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Female_raw_sig =
      !is.na(p_detect_age_Female) &
        p_detect_age_Female <=
          0.05,

    Male_raw_sig =
      !is.na(p_detect_age_Male) &
        p_detect_age_Male <=
          0.05,

    Female_FDR_sig =
      !is.na(FDR_detect_Female) &
        FDR_detect_Female <=
          0.05,

    Male_FDR_sig =
      !is.na(FDR_detect_Male) &
        FDR_detect_Male <=
          0.05,

    Fisher_pattern =
      case_when(
        Female_raw_sig &
          Male_raw_sig ~
          "Both sexes p <= 0.05",

        Female_raw_sig &
          !Male_raw_sig ~
          "Female p <= 0.05 only",

        !Female_raw_sig &
          Male_raw_sig ~
          "Male p <= 0.05 only",

        TRUE ~
          "NS"
      ),

    Sex_difference_delta =
      delta_prev_Male -
      delta_prev_Female,

    Abs_sex_difference_delta =
      abs(Sex_difference_delta),

    Any_oldpred =
      replace_na(old_predominant_Female, FALSE) |
        replace_na(old_predominant_Male, FALSE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(pmin(p_detect_age_Female, p_detect_age_Male, na.rm = TRUE), desc(Abs_sex_difference_delta))

# Plotting universe: union of the Female and Male Old-predominant lists.
# This preserves the full detect_female_male object for downstream compact
# matrix analyses while ensuring the delta plot matches the complete lists.
detect_female_male_plot <- detect_female_male %>%
  mutate(
    old_predominant_Female =
      tidyr::replace_na(old_predominant_Female, FALSE),

    old_predominant_Male =
      tidyr::replace_na(old_predominant_Male, FALSE)
  ) %>%
  filter(old_predominant_Female | old_predominant_Male)

write.csv(
  detect_female_male_plot,
  file.path(split_detect_dir, "DetectionDelta_Female_vs_Male.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r detection-female-male-scatter, fig.keep="none"}
# ==============================================================================
# Adult-vs-Old Female/Male detection delta scatter
#
# Circle   = Female
# Triangle = Male
#
# Open   = NS
# Filled = raw Fisher p ≤ 0.05
#
# Color = cellular component
#
# A symbol is shown ONLY if the protein meets the Old-predominant criterion
# in that sex.
#
# Proteins with identical Female/Male delta coordinates receive a very small
# deterministic visual displacement. Significant labels are anchored to the
# actual displayed significant symbol.
# ==============================================================================

base_delta_df <- detect_female_male_plot %>%

  filter(is.finite(delta_prev_Female), is.finite(delta_prev_Male)) %>%

  mutate(
    Female_member =
      tidyr::replace_na(old_predominant_Female, FALSE),

    Male_member =
      tidyr::replace_na(old_predominant_Male, FALSE)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Protein-level displacement for exact coordinate ties
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

jitter_radius <- 0.026

delta_jitter_tbl <- base_delta_df %>%

  distinct(Protein.Group, Gene1, delta_prev_Female, delta_prev_Male) %>%

  arrange(delta_prev_Female, delta_prev_Male, Gene1, Protein.Group) %>%

  group_by(delta_prev_Female, delta_prev_Male) %>%

  mutate(
    overlap_n =
      n(),

    overlap_index =
      row_number(),

    jitter_angle =
      if_else(overlap_n > 1, 2 * pi * (overlap_index - 1) / overlap_n, 0),

    protein_jitter_x =
      if_else(overlap_n > 1, jitter_radius * cos(jitter_angle), 0),

    protein_jitter_y =
      if_else(overlap_n > 1, jitter_radius * sin(jitter_angle), 0)
  ) %>%

  ungroup() %>%

  select(Protein.Group, protein_jitter_x, protein_jitter_y, overlap_n)

base_delta_df <- base_delta_df %>%

  left_join(delta_jitter_tbl, by = "Protein.Group")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Small sex-specific separation when the same protein is Old-predominant
# in both Female and Male mice
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

sex_offset <- 0.012

female_symbol_df <- base_delta_df %>%

  filter(Female_member) %>%

  transmute(
    Protein.Group,
    Gene1,
    Bin,

    True_x =
      delta_prev_Female,

    True_y =
      delta_prev_Male,

    Plot_x =
      delta_prev_Female +
      protein_jitter_x -
      sex_offset,

    Plot_y =
      delta_prev_Male +
      protein_jitter_y +
      sex_offset,

    Sex =
      "Female",

    Significant =
      tidyr::replace_na(Female_raw_sig, FALSE)
  )

male_symbol_df <- base_delta_df %>%

  filter(Male_member) %>%

  transmute(
    Protein.Group,
    Gene1,
    Bin,

    True_x =
      delta_prev_Female,

    True_y =
      delta_prev_Male,

    Plot_x =
      delta_prev_Female +
      protein_jitter_x +
      sex_offset,

    Plot_y =
      delta_prev_Male +
      protein_jitter_y -
      sex_offset,

    Sex =
      "Male",

    Significant =
      tidyr::replace_na(Male_raw_sig, FALSE)
  )

delta_symbol_df <- bind_rows(female_symbol_df, male_symbol_df) %>%

  mutate(
    SymbolClass = case_when(

      Sex ==
        "Female" &
        !Significant ~
        "Female — NS",

      Sex ==
        "Female" &
        Significant ~
        "Female — p ≤ 0.05",

      Sex ==
        "Male" &
        !Significant ~
        "Male — NS",

      Sex ==
        "Male" &
        Significant ~
        "Male — p ≤ 0.05"
    ),

    SymbolClass = factor(
      SymbolClass,
      levels = c("Female — NS", "Female — p ≤ 0.05", "Male — NS", "Male — p ≤ 0.05")
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Significant labels:
# anchor each label to the actual displayed significant symbol.
# If significant in both sexes, use the midpoint of the two displayed symbols.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

detection_scatter_labels <- delta_symbol_df %>%

  filter(Significant) %>%

  group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin) %>%

  summarise(label_x = mean(Plot_x, na.rm = TRUE), label_y = mean(Plot_y, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Only cellular components represented in this figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

delta_bins_present <- dot_bin_order[dot_bin_order %in% unique(as.character(delta_symbol_df$Bin))]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

p_detection_female_male <- ggplot() +

  geom_abline(
    slope = 1,
    intercept = 0,
    linetype = "dotted",
    colour = "grey35",
    linewidth = nm_style$detection_reference_line
  ) +

  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey72",
    linewidth = nm_style$detection_reference_line
  ) +

  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey72",
    linewidth = nm_style$detection_reference_line
  ) +

  # Female — NS = open circle
  geom_point(
    data =
      delta_symbol_df %>%
      filter(SymbolClass == "Female — NS"),

    aes(x = Plot_x, y = Plot_y, colour = Bin, shape = SymbolClass),

    size = nm_style$detection_point_open,
    stroke = nm_style$detection_point_stroke
  ) +

  # Female — significant = filled circle
  geom_point(
    data =
      delta_symbol_df %>%
      filter(SymbolClass == "Female — p ≤ 0.05"),

    aes(x = Plot_x, y = Plot_y, colour = Bin, shape = SymbolClass),

    size = nm_style$detection_point_filled,
    stroke = nm_style$detection_point_stroke
  ) +

  # Male — NS = open triangle
  geom_point(
    data =
      delta_symbol_df %>%
      filter(SymbolClass == "Male — NS"),

    aes(x = Plot_x, y = Plot_y, colour = Bin, shape = SymbolClass),

    size = nm_style$detection_point_open,
    stroke = nm_style$detection_point_stroke
  ) +

  # Male — significant = filled triangle
  geom_point(
    data =
      delta_symbol_df %>%
      filter(SymbolClass == "Male — p ≤ 0.05"),

    aes(x = Plot_x, y = Plot_y, colour = Bin, shape = SymbolClass),

    size = nm_style$detection_point_filled,
    stroke = nm_style$detection_point_stroke
  ) +

  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    data =
      detection_scatter_labels,

    aes(x = label_x, y = label_y, label = Gene1, colour = Bin),

    size = nm_style$detection_label_pt / ggplot2::.pt,

    box.padding = nm_style$detection_label_padding,
    point.padding = nm_style$detection_label_padding,

    force = 2,

    min.segment.length = 0,

    segment.size = nm_style$detection_label_segment,
    segment.colour = "grey45",

    max.overlaps = Inf,

    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("Female — NS" = 1, "Female — p ≤ 0.05" = 16, "Male — NS" = 2, "Male — p ≤ 0.05" = 17),

    limits = c("Female — NS", "Female — p ≤ 0.05", "Male — NS", "Male — p ≤ 0.05"),

    drop = FALSE,

    name =
      "Sex / Fisher test"
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(
    values =
      bin_pal_dot[delta_bins_present],

    breaks =
      delta_bins_present,

    limits =
      delta_bins_present,

    drop = FALSE,

    name =
      "Cellular component"
  ) +

  guides(
    shape = guide_legend(
      order = 1,

      override.aes = list(colour = "black", size = nm_style$detection_point_open, alpha = 1)
    ),

    colour = guide_legend(
      order = 2,

      override.aes = list(shape = 16, size = nm_style$detection_point_filled, alpha = 1)
    )
  ) +

  coord_equal(xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1), clip = "off") +

  labs(
    title =
      "Proteins with Old-predominant detection",

    subtitle =
      "Dotted y = x indicates identical age-associated change between female and male",

    x =
      "Female change in detection (Old − Adult)",

    y =
      "Male change in detection (Old − Adult)"
  ) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 12.5) +

  theme(
    plot.title =
      element_text(face = "bold", size = nm_style$axis_title),

    plot.subtitle =
      element_text(colour = "grey35", size = nm_style$small_text),

    legend.position =
      "right",

    legend.box =
      "vertical",

    legend.text =
      element_text(size = nm_style$legend_text),

    plot.margin =
      margin(10, 15, 15, 10)
  )

detection_female_male_png <- file.path(split_detect_dir, "DetectionDelta_Female_vs_Male.png")

save_plot_png(p_detection_female_male, detection_female_male_png, width = 9.3, height = 7.5, dpi = 300)

# QC table: these sex/component counts should match the complete
# Female/Male Old-predominant lists above.
delta_symbol_df %>%

  count(Sex, Bin, name = "n_symbols") %>%

  arrange(Sex, factor(Bin, levels = dot_bin_order))
```

### Alternative protein-wise delta plot

As an alternative to the Female-versus-Male delta scatter, this view places each Old-predominant protein on a separate row. A symbol is shown only for the sex in which that protein meets the Old-predominant criterion, using the same circle/triangle and open/filled encoding as the delta scatter.

```{r alternative-proteinwise-age-delta, fig.keep="none"}
proteinwise_age_df <- detect_bysex_all %>%

  filter(old_predominant, Bin %in% dot_bin_order) %>%

  transmute(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Sex = as.character(Sex), Delta = delta_prev, Fisher_p = p_detect_age) %>%

  mutate(
    Significant =
      !is.na(Fisher_p) &
        Fisher_p <=
          0.05,

    SymbolClass = case_when(

      Sex ==
        "Female" &
        !Significant ~
        "Female — NS",

      Sex ==
        "Female" &
        Significant ~
        "Female — p ≤ 0.05",

      Sex ==
        "Male" &
        !Significant ~
        "Male — NS",

      Sex ==
        "Male" &
        Significant ~
        "Male — p ≤ 0.05"
    ),

    SymbolClass = factor(
      SymbolClass,
      levels = c("Female — NS", "Female — p ≤ 0.05", "Male — NS", "Male — p ≤ 0.05")
    )
  )

proteinwise_age_order <- proteinwise_age_df %>%

  group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin) %>%

  summarise(Mean_delta = mean(Delta, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%

  arrange(factor(Bin, levels = dot_bin_order), Mean_delta) %>%

  mutate(ProteinLabel = make.unique(as.character(Gene1)))

proteinwise_age_df <- proteinwise_age_df %>%

  left_join(proteinwise_age_order %>% select(Protein.Group, ProteinLabel), by = "Protein.Group") %>%

  mutate(ProteinLabel = factor(ProteinLabel, levels = rev(proteinwise_age_order$ProteinLabel)))
```

### Compact four-group detection matrix for selected candidates

This display retains the actual Adult Female, Old Female, Adult Male, and Old Male detection prevalences but limits the rows to the strongest candidates.

Selection prioritizes:

1. proteins with raw within-sex Fisher `p <= 0.05` in either sex;
2. then other Old-predominant proteins with the largest detection shifts, if space remains.

The default maximum is 18 proteins. This number can be changed with `max_detection_matrix_proteins`.

Dot size represents detection prevalence. A grey X indicates zero detection.

```{r selected-detection-matrix-data}
max_detection_matrix_proteins <- 18

candidate_ranking <- detect_female_male %>%
  mutate(
    Any_raw_sig =
      Female_raw_sig |
        Male_raw_sig,

    Any_oldpred =
      replace_na(old_predominant_Female, FALSE) |
        replace_na(old_predominant_Male, FALSE),

    min_raw_p = pmin(p_detect_age_Female, p_detect_age_Male, na.rm = TRUE),

    max_positive_delta = pmax(delta_prev_Female, delta_prev_Male, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  filter(Any_raw_sig | Any_oldpred) %>%
  arrange(desc(Any_raw_sig), min_raw_p, desc(max_positive_delta), desc(Abs_sex_difference_delta)) %>%
  slice_head(n = max_detection_matrix_proteins) %>%
  mutate(
    Selection_rank =
      row_number(),

    Selection_reason =
      case_when(
        Female_raw_sig &
          Male_raw_sig ~
          "Raw p <= 0.05 in both sexes",

        Female_raw_sig ~
          "Raw p <= 0.05 in Female",

        Male_raw_sig ~
          "Raw p <= 0.05 in Male",

        Any_oldpred ~
          "Old-predominant candidate",

        TRUE ~
          "Other"
      ),

    GeneLabel =
      make.unique(as.character(Gene1))
  )

write.csv(
  candidate_ranking,
  file.path(split_detect_dir, "Detection_SelectedCandidates_ranking.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

selected_detection_matrix <- bind_rows(

  candidate_ranking %>%
    transmute(
      Protein.Group,
      Gene1,
      GeneLabel,
      Bin,
      Selection_rank,
      Selection_reason,
      Group =
        "Adult_Female",
      detected_n =
        adult_detected_n_Female,
      total_n =
        adult_total_n_Female,
      prevalence =
        adult_prev_Female
    ),

  candidate_ranking %>%
    transmute(
      Protein.Group,
      Gene1,
      GeneLabel,
      Bin,
      Selection_rank,
      Selection_reason,
      Group =
        "Old_Female",
      detected_n =
        old_detected_n_Female,
      total_n =
        old_total_n_Female,
      prevalence =
        old_prev_Female
    ),

  candidate_ranking %>%
    transmute(
      Protein.Group,
      Gene1,
      GeneLabel,
      Bin,
      Selection_rank,
      Selection_reason,
      Group =
        "Adult_Male",
      detected_n =
        adult_detected_n_Male,
      total_n =
        adult_total_n_Male,
      prevalence =
        adult_prev_Male
    ),

  candidate_ranking %>%
    transmute(
      Protein.Group,
      Gene1,
      GeneLabel,
      Bin,
      Selection_rank,
      Selection_reason,
      Group =
        "Old_Male",
      detected_n =
        old_detected_n_Male,
      total_n =
        old_total_n_Male,
      prevalence =
        old_prev_Male
    )
) %>%
  mutate(
    Group = factor(Group, levels = c("Adult_Female", "Old_Female", "Adult_Male", "Old_Male")),

    GeneLabel = factor(GeneLabel, levels = rev(candidate_ranking$GeneLabel)),

    prevalence_label =
      sprintf("%d/%d", detected_n, total_n)
  )

write.csv(
  selected_detection_matrix,
  file.path(split_detect_dir, "Detection_SelectedCandidates_4GroupMatrix.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# Heatmap and centered-abundance alternatives

The four-group bubble plot encodes absolute abundance by circle size, which can make modest differences difficult to judge. The next two heatmaps display the **pooled Old-ranked Top-10 proteins** across the same four Age × Sex groups using color-based abundance scales.

The two heatmaps answer different questions:

1. **Absolute abundance heatmap:** preserves between-protein abundance differences using `log10(mean intensity)`.
2. **Within-protein centered heatmap:** emphasizes whether a particular protein is relatively higher or lower in Adult Female, Old Female, Adult Male, or Old Male muscle.

The centered heatmap is not a Z-score. For each protein, the mean of the available group-level `log10(mean intensity)` values is subtracted from each Age × Sex group value:

`centered log10 abundance = group log10(mean intensity) − protein mean log10(mean intensity across groups)`.

Thus, zero represents that protein's own across-group mean, positive values indicate relatively higher abundance, and negative values indicate relatively lower abundance. Because values are not divided by the protein-specific standard deviation, the scale remains a log10 difference rather than a standardized Z-score. Missing groups remain `ND` rather than being imputed.

## Prepare heatmap data

```{r top10-heatmap-data}
top10_heatmap_tbl <- pooled_top10_bysex %>%
  mutate(
    log10_intensity = if_else(!is.na(mean_intensity) & mean_intensity > 0, log10(mean_intensity), NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Protein.Group) %>%
  mutate(
    protein_mean_log10 = if_else(any(is.finite(log10_intensity)), mean(log10_intensity, na.rm = TRUE), NA_real_),

    centered_log10 = if_else(
      is.finite(log10_intensity) &
        is.finite(protein_mean_log10),
      log10_intensity -
        protein_mean_log10,
      NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

write.csv(
  top10_heatmap_tbl,
  file.path(split_dot_dir, "Top10_PooledOldRank_bySex_heatmap_values.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

absolute_limits <- range(top10_heatmap_tbl$log10_intensity, na.rm = TRUE)

center_abs_max <- max(abs(top10_heatmap_tbl$centered_log10), na.rm = TRUE)

if (!is.finite(center_abs_max) || center_abs_max == 0) {
  center_abs_max <- 1
}
```
## Absolute abundance heatmap

The same color scale is used across all cellular components. Consequently, proteins that are intrinsically much more abundant retain stronger absolute-abundance values than lower-abundance proteins; the colors are not normalized separately by component.

Grey cells labeled `ND` indicate that the protein was not detected in that Age × Sex group.

```{r absolute-heatmap, fig.keep="none"}
absolute_heatmap_list <- list()

for (i in seq_along(dot_bin_order)) {

  bin_name <- dot_bin_order[i]
  bin_col  <- bin_pal_dot[[bin_name]]

  rank_tbl <- pooled_top10 %>%
    filter(Bin == bin_name) %>%
    arrange(desc(pooled_Old_mean)) %>%
    mutate(GeneLabel = make.unique(as.character(Gene1)))

  plot_df <- top10_heatmap_tbl %>%
    filter(Bin == bin_name) %>%
    left_join(rank_tbl %>% select(Protein.Group, GeneLabel), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
    mutate(GeneLabel = factor(GeneLabel, levels = rev(rank_tbl$GeneLabel)))

  if (nrow(plot_df) == 0) {
    next
  }

  p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Group, y = GeneLabel, fill = log10_intensity)) +

    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.55) +

    geom_text(
      data = plot_df %>%
        filter(is.na(log10_intensity)),
      aes(label = "ND"),
      colour = "grey55",
      size = 2.4
    ) +

    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      option = "C",
      limits = absolute_limits,
      oob = scales::squish,
      na.value = "grey95",
      name = expression(log[10]("mean intensity"))
    ) +

    scale_x_discrete(
      position = "top",
      labels = c(
        "Adult_Female" = "Adult\nF",
        "Old_Female"   = "Old\nF",
        "Adult_Male"   = "Adult\nM",
        "Old_Male"     = "Old\nM"
      )
    ) +

    labs(title = bin_name, x = NULL, y = NULL) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +

    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = nm_style$dot_protein_title_pt, colour = bin_col),

      axis.text.x = element_text(size = nm_style$dot_group_label_pt, face = "bold"),

      axis.text.y = element_text(size = nm_style$dot_protein_label_pt),

      axis.line = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),

      legend.position = if (i == 1) {
        "right"
      } else {
        "none"
      },

      plot.margin = margin(6, 8, 6, 8)
    )

  absolute_heatmap_list[[bin_name]] <- p
}

absolute_heatmap_combined <-
  patchwork::wrap_plots(plotlist = absolute_heatmap_list, ncol = 4) +

  patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") +

  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title =
      "Absolute abundance of the most abundant insoluble proteins",

    subtitle =
      "Pooled Old-ranked Top 10 proteins; fill = log10(mean intensity)",

    theme =
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 7.5, hjust = 0.5),

        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 5.5, colour = "grey35", hjust = 0.5)
      )
  ) &

  theme(legend.position = "right")

absolute_heatmap_png <- file.path(split_dot_dir, "Top10_PooledOldRank_bySex_AbsoluteHeatmap.png")

if (file.exists(absolute_heatmap_png)) {
  unlink(absolute_heatmap_png)
}
```

## Within-protein centered abundance heatmap

This version suppresses the very large differences in baseline abundance between proteins and emphasizes the **pattern across the four Age × Sex groups for each protein**.

For example:

- positive values = higher than that protein's own four-group mean
- negative values = lower than that protein's own four-group mean
- zero = approximately equal to that protein's four-group mean

Because this is centered but **not divided by the protein-specific standard deviation**, the magnitude still represents a difference in `log10` abundance rather than an arbitrary Z-score.

```{r centered-heatmap, fig.keep="none"}
centered_heatmap_list <- list()

for (i in seq_along(dot_bin_order)) {

  bin_name <- dot_bin_order[i]
  bin_col  <- bin_pal_dot[[bin_name]]

  rank_tbl <- pooled_top10 %>%
    filter(Bin == bin_name) %>%
    arrange(desc(pooled_Old_mean)) %>%
    mutate(GeneLabel = make.unique(as.character(Gene1)))

  plot_df <- top10_heatmap_tbl %>%
    filter(Bin == bin_name) %>%
    left_join(rank_tbl %>% select(Protein.Group, GeneLabel), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
    mutate(GeneLabel = factor(GeneLabel, levels = rev(rank_tbl$GeneLabel)))

  if (nrow(plot_df) == 0) {
    next
  }

  p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Group, y = GeneLabel, fill = centered_log10)) +

    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.55) +

    geom_text(data = plot_df %>% filter(is.na(centered_log10)), aes(label = "ND"), colour = "grey55", size = 2.4) +

    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = "#3B528B",
      mid = "white",
      high = "#D62728",
      midpoint = 0,
      limits = c(-center_abs_max, center_abs_max),
      oob = scales::squish,
      na.value = "grey95",
      name = expression(Delta ~ log[10]("intensity"))
    ) +

    scale_x_discrete(
      position = "top",
      labels = c(
        "Adult_Female" = "Adult\nF",
        "Old_Female"   = "Old\nF",
        "Adult_Male"   = "Adult\nM",
        "Old_Male"     = "Old\nM"
      )
    ) +

    labs(title = bin_name, x = NULL, y = NULL) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +

    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = nm_style$dot_protein_title_pt, colour = bin_col),

      axis.text.x = element_text(size = nm_style$dot_group_label_pt, face = "bold"),

      axis.text.y = element_text(size = nm_style$dot_protein_label_pt),

      axis.line = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),

      legend.position = if (i == 1) {
        "right"
      } else {
        "none"
      },

      plot.margin = margin(6, 8, 6, 8)
    )

  centered_heatmap_list[[bin_name]] <- p
}

centered_heatmap_combined <-
  patchwork::wrap_plots(plotlist = centered_heatmap_list, ncol = 4) +

  patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") +

  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title =
      "Relative abundance across age and sex",

    subtitle =
      "Within-protein centered log10(mean intensity); red = relatively higher, blue = relatively lower",

    theme =
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 7.5, hjust = 0.5),

        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 5.5, colour = "grey35", hjust = 0.5)
      )
  ) &

  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

## Within-protein centered bubble plots (Top 10 and Top 5)

This figure shows the same centered values as the preceding heatmap, but with:

- **color** = direction relative to that protein's own four-group mean
  - red = relatively higher
  - blue = relatively lower
- **bubble size** = absolute magnitude of that deviation
- **grey X** = not detected

Bubble size here does **not** represent absolute protein abundance.

The Top-10 view includes all ten Old-ranked proteins per component. The separate
Top-5 view selects the five highest-ranked proteins **from those same Old pooled
rankings**, retaining their precomputed four-group centered values. Both plots
use the same numerical color limits; only the rendered bubble sizes differ.

```{r centered-bubble-plot, fig.keep="none"}
centered_bubble_list <- list()

bubble_mag_max <- max(abs(top10_heatmap_tbl$centered_log10), na.rm = TRUE)

if (!is.finite(bubble_mag_max) || bubble_mag_max == 0) {
  bubble_mag_max <- 1
}

bubble_size_breaks <- pretty(c(0, bubble_mag_max), n = 4)

bubble_size_breaks <- bubble_size_breaks[bubble_size_breaks >= 0 & bubble_size_breaks <= bubble_mag_max]

for (i in seq_along(dot_bin_order)) {

  bin_name <- dot_bin_order[i]
  bin_col  <- bin_pal_dot[[bin_name]]

  rank_tbl <- pooled_top10 %>%
    filter(Bin == bin_name) %>%
    arrange(desc(pooled_Old_mean)) %>%
    mutate(GeneLabel = make.unique(as.character(Gene1)))

  plot_df <- top10_heatmap_tbl %>%
    filter(Bin == bin_name) %>%
    left_join(rank_tbl %>% dplyr::select(Protein.Group, GeneLabel), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
    mutate(
      GeneLabel = factor(GeneLabel, levels = rev(rank_tbl$GeneLabel)),

      deviation_magnitude =
        abs(centered_log10)
    )

  if (nrow(plot_df) == 0) {
    next
  }

  row_guides <- tibble(GeneLabel = levels(plot_df$GeneLabel))

  p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Group, y = GeneLabel)) +

    geom_segment(
      data = row_guides,
      aes(x = 0.65, xend = 4.35, y = GeneLabel, yend = GeneLabel),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      colour = "grey93",
      linewidth = nm_style$centered_bubble_grid_line
    ) +

    geom_vline(xintercept = 1:4, colour = "grey94", linewidth = nm_style$centered_bubble_grid_line) +

    geom_point(
      data = plot_df %>%
        filter(!is.na(centered_log10)),
      aes(size = deviation_magnitude, colour = centered_log10),
      alpha = 0.92
    ) +

    geom_point(
      data = plot_df %>%
        filter(is.na(centered_log10)),
      shape = 4,
      size = nm_style$centered_bubble_missing_mm,
      stroke = nm_style$centered_bubble_missing_stroke,
      colour = "grey65"
    ) +

    scale_colour_gradient2(
      low = "#3B528B",
      mid = "grey92",
      high = "#D62728",
      midpoint = 0,
      limits = c(-bubble_mag_max, bubble_mag_max),
      oob = scales::squish,
      name = expression(Delta ~ log[10]("intensity"))
    ) +

    scale_size_continuous(
      range = c(nm_style$centered_bubble_min_mm, nm_style$centered_bubble_max_mm),
      limits = c(0, bubble_mag_max),
      breaks =
        bubble_size_breaks,
      name =
        "|centered value|"
    ) +

    scale_x_discrete(
      position = "top",
      labels = c(
        "Adult_Female" =
          "Adult\nF",
        "Old_Female" =
          "Old\nF",
        "Adult_Male" =
          "Adult\nM",
        "Old_Male" =
          "Old\nM"
      )
    ) +

    labs(title = bin_name, x = NULL, y = NULL) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +

    theme(
      plot.title =
        element_text(face = "bold", size = nm_style$centered_bubble_component_pt, colour = bin_col),
      axis.text.x =
        element_text(size = nm_style$centered_bubble_group_pt, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y =
        element_text(size = nm_style$centered_bubble_protein_pt),
      axis.line =
        element_blank(),
      axis.ticks =
        element_blank(),
      panel.grid =
        element_blank(),
      legend.position =
        if (i == 1) {
          "right"
        } else {
          "none"
        },
      plot.margin =
        margin(1, 2, 1, 2)
    )

  centered_bubble_list[[bin_name]] <- p
}

centered_bubble_combined <-
  patchwork::wrap_plots(plotlist = centered_bubble_list, ncol = 4) +

  patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") +

  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title =
      "Relative abundance across age and sex",
    subtitle =
      paste0(
        "Within-protein centered log10(mean intensity); ",
        "size = magnitude of deviation; ",
        "red = relatively higher, blue = relatively lower"
      ),
    theme =
      theme(
        plot.title =
          element_text(face = "bold", size = 7.5, hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle =
          element_text(size = 5.5, colour = "grey35", hjust = 0.5)
      )
  ) &

  theme(legend.position = "right")

centered_bubble_png <- file.path(split_dot_dir, "Top10_PooledOldRank_bySex_CenteredBubbles.png")

if (file.exists(centered_bubble_png)) {
  unlink(centered_bubble_png)
}

save_plot_png(centered_bubble_combined, centered_bubble_png, width = 120 / 25.4, height = 80 / 25.4, dpi = 300)
```

```{r show-centered-bubbles, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
if (file.exists(centered_bubble_png)) {
  knitr::include_graphics(centered_bubble_png)
}
```
## Top-5 pooled Old-ranked centered bubble plot (Figure 3 companion)

This additional figure uses the five highest pooled Old-abundance proteins
within each cellular component. The underlying within-protein centered values
are identical to the Top-10 analysis; group means and missing detections are not
recomputed. The Top-10 figure is retained separately.

```{r centered-bubble-top5-plot, fig.keep="none"}
# Requires: pooled_top10, top10_heatmap_tbl, dot_bin_order, bin_pal_dot,
# and the centered-bubble-plot chunk (for bubble_mag_max / breaks).
stopifnot(exists("pooled_top10"), exists("top10_heatmap_tbl"),
          exists("bubble_mag_max"), exists("bubble_size_breaks"))

centered_top5_panels <- list()

for (bin_name in dot_bin_order) {
  rank5 <- pooled_top10 %>%
    dplyr::filter(Bin == bin_name) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(pooled_Old_mean)) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 5L) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(GeneLabel = make.unique(as.character(Gene1)))

  if (nrow(rank5) == 0L) next

  dat5 <- top10_heatmap_tbl %>%
    dplyr::filter(Bin == bin_name, Protein.Group %in% rank5$Protein.Group) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(rank5 %>% dplyr::select(Protein.Group, GeneLabel), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      GeneLabel = factor(GeneLabel, levels = rev(rank5$GeneLabel)),
      deviation_magnitude = abs(centered_log10)
    )

  if (nrow(dat5) == 0L) next

  row5 <- tibble::tibble(GeneLabel = levels(dat5$GeneLabel))

  p5 <- ggplot2::ggplot(dat5, ggplot2::aes(x = Group, y = GeneLabel)) +
    ggplot2::geom_segment(
      data = row5,
      ggplot2::aes(x = 0.65, xend = 4.35, y = GeneLabel, yend = GeneLabel),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      colour = "grey93", linewidth = nm_style$centered_bubble_grid_line
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 1:4, colour = "grey94", linewidth = nm_style$centered_bubble_grid_line) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = dat5 %>% dplyr::filter(is.finite(centered_log10)),
      ggplot2::aes(size = deviation_magnitude, colour = centered_log10),
      alpha = 0.92
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = dat5 %>% dplyr::filter(!is.finite(centered_log10)),
      shape = 4, size = nm_style$centered_top5_missing_mm,
      stroke = nm_style$centered_bubble_missing_stroke,
      colour = "grey65"
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_gradient2(
      low = "#3B528B", mid = "grey92", high = "#D62728",
      midpoint = 0, limits = c(-bubble_mag_max, bubble_mag_max),
      oob = scales::squish,
      name = expression(Delta ~ log[10]("intensity"))
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_size_continuous(
      range = c(nm_style$centered_top5_min_mm, nm_style$centered_top5_max_mm),
      limits = c(0, bubble_mag_max), breaks = bubble_size_breaks,
      name = "|centered value|"
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(
      position = "top",
      labels = c("Adult_Female" = "Adult\nF",
                 "Old_Female" = "Old\nF",
                 "Adult_Male" = "Adult\nM",
                 "Old_Male" = "Old\nM")
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(title = bin_name, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 8) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold", size = nm_style$centered_top5_component_pt,
        colour = bin_pal_dot[[bin_name]]
      ),
      axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = nm_style$centered_top5_group_pt, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = nm_style$centered_top5_protein_pt),
      axis.line = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      legend.position = "right",
      plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(1, 1, 1, 1)
    )

  centered_top5_panels[[bin_name]] <- p5
}

# No overall title/subtitle: retain only the colored component headings.
centered_top5_combined <- patchwork::wrap_plots(plotlist = centered_top5_panels, ncol = 4) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "right")

centered_top5_png <- file.path(split_dot_dir, "Top5_PooledOldRank_bySex_CenteredBubbles.png")
save_plot_png(
  centered_top5_combined,
  centered_top5_png,
  width = nm_dims$Top5_PooledOldRank_bySex_CenteredBubbles[["width"]] / 25.4,
  height = nm_dims$Top5_PooledOldRank_bySex_CenteredBubbles[["height"]] / 25.4,
  dpi = nm_export$dpi
)
```

```{r show-centered-top5-bubbles, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
if (file.exists(centered_top5_png)) knitr::include_graphics(centered_top5_png)
```

The report intentionally does **not** create the protein-level Female-versus-Male insoluble-abundance age-effect scatter or rerun protein-level insoluble limma differential abundance. Those analyses are maintained in the dedicated Insoluble report.
